The `CFG_EVENT_CREATE_AUDIO_PATCH` line in the same block\nrecords each route change with a timestamp, so it also answers what happened mid-take.\n\n## FACT: what-the-2026-09-03-silence-run-proved-and-what-it-did-not\nThe #5 auto-stop run on the S26, debug build, phone SECURE-LOCKED (everything below needs no screen).\n\n- `getMinBufferSize` returns **1280** bytes for 16 kHz mono PCM16, so the 32,000-byte floor binds\n  (`Buffer sizes: minimum=1280 coerced=32000 read=8192`); the one-second read granularity the change\n  removed was real.\n- The detector runs in `com.envi.wispr:vad` by PID and exits when the last client unbinds.\n- **Killing the detector mid-recording does not disturb the recording**: `run-as com.envi.wispr kill -9\n  <vad-pid>`, then `:audio` logged `Auto-stop abandoned for this take` and the take ran to 12.0 s.\n  `run-as com.envi.wispr.test` CANNOT kill a `com.envi.wispr` process (different UID, `kill` returns 1,\n  the test still passes); re-read the pid after any kill.\n- **A quiet room never ends a take** (12.0 s, `TERMINAL_REASON_MANUAL`): the control that matters most.\n- Also proven over the real binder: real speech scores CONTINUE and the silence after it ends the take,\n  not on the first silent block; a start from an older take is refused outright and its blocks with it;\n  a wrongly sized block is refused; the switch off means no\n  detector; an out-of-range pause refuses auto-stop while recording continues.\n- **Same evening, unlocked, founder's hand:** a silence-ended take inserted into Gmail (6.4 s, 43\n  characters, `handoff=SCHEDULED`) and WhatsApp; the switch and slider survive a restart and an install.\n  Receipt: `.validation/runs/20260904T004512Z-53755bb`.\n\n**The stop line names the ending** (`endTakeLocked` writes `Stopped by <ending>.`; the time limit and a\ncapture failure write their own lines from `captureLoop`). Never read the ORDER of log lines:\n`claimEnding` clears `isRecording` before `recording_stop`, so a silence stop and a button press log in the\nsame order. `a stop request` is NOT proof the user pressed stop (`onDestroy` ends a take by the same\nroute); telling them apart needs a new AIDL reason (#114).\n\n**A Gmail window opened over ADB does not pin** (`NO_PINNED_TARGET` on the branch AND on `main`), the same\nartifact as FACT: what-gmail-actually-does-to-insertion-2026-08-30; two runs are comparable only when the\neditor was opened the same way.\n\n## FACT: the-polish-policy-propagation-uat\nThe recipe for #69, and for any change to how the engine learns the polish mode. The oracle is PID\nEQUALITY plus the load line: a fresh pid proves nothing, and the buggy code printed no load line at all.\n\n1. AI Polish saved as Off. Start a dictation and cancel it (`am start -n com.envi.wispr/.ui.VoiceInputActivity\n   --ez toggle true`, then `--ez cancel true`), so the engine process is alive: `pidof com.envi.wispr:polish`.\n2. Switch to This phone on the screen. Dictate into Samsung Notes. `logcat -s PolishService` must show\n   `S1-mini loaded` on the SAME pid, and the History card must read \"Polished by S1-mini by Superwhisper\".\n3. Switch to a cloud provider with a saved key; dictate; the History card names the provider.\n4. Switch back to Off; dictate; the History card reads \"AI Polish was off\".\nNo app kill between steps. Restore the mode the phone had before the run.\n\n## FACT: the-residency-campaign\n`scripts/uat/residency-campaign.sh <runs> <short.pcm> <long.pcm>` is the #72 measurement: real dictations\nthrough the speaker in four warm-up shapes × rested and loaded memory, with an on-device sampler\n(`scripts/uat/device-sampler.sh`) and `scripts/uat/residency-report.py` for the table. It refuses a phone it\ncannot measure honestly and restores the override file and the screen timeout from a trap. Traps it was\nbuilt around, each measured 2026-09-01:\n\n- **A Bluetooth headset steals the speaker**, so the fixture plays into the founder's ears and the phone\n  hears nothing: the transcript comes back empty and the run looks like an ASR failure.\n- **`grep -q` under `pipefail` refuses on a MATCH** (`../rules/validation-discipline.md` FACT:\n  silent-empty-traps): the preflight refused an awake phone until every probe captured its output first.\n- **The screen timeout ends the campaign silently.** A dimmed phone is woken with `KEYCODE_WAKEUP`; a\n  locked one is refused (FACT above). The script raises the timeout to thirty minutes and restores it.\n- **The stratum is derived, never labelled.** `am kill` before a cold run must leave no `:polish` pid, and\n  the report classifies cold versus cached from the pid recorded before the run.\n- **The spoken fixture comes from Azure Speech** (`phone-audio-playback.md`); the eleven-second one yields\n  about 175 characters, so a transcript outside 120 to 260 characters marks the run failed rather than\n  averaged.\n\n## FACT: the-staged-polish-timeout\nLocal polish has an engine deadline and the session a watchdog (#75). Neither can be staged with a real\nwedge, so a debug build reads two per-request files under `files/debug/` (integers in milliseconds,\ndebuggable builds only, out-of-range values ignored): `polish-deadline-ms` replaces the cooperative\ndeadline (hard = value + 2 s), and `polish-stall-ms` holds the worker BEFORE generation, outside the\ncooperative timeout, which is what a wedge looks like. Recipe, This phone selected, fixture in place\n(`phone-audio-playback.md`), `scripts/uat/dictate-once.sh` for each dictation:\n\n1. Cooperative path: `run-as com.envi.wispr sh -c 'mkdir -p files/debug && printf 1 > files/debug/polish-deadline-ms'`.\n   Expect `reason=LOCAL_TIMEOUT`, `engine process will end`, the deterministic text handed off, `Ending the\n   polish engine process` within a second, `pidof com.envi.wispr:polish` empty. Remove the file and dictate\n   again: `Ready on GPU` on a NEW pid and `reason=POLISHED`. Measured 2026-09-01: expiry to exit 81 ms.\n2. Hard path: `printf 30000 > files/debug/polish-stall-ms` with no deadline file. Expect the shipped hard\n   timer at 12 s: `Local polish deadline expired` while the worker is still asleep, then the exit; the\n   session receives `LOCAL_TIMEOUT` before its own 15 s watchdog. Measured 2026-09-01: expiry at\n   12.0 s from the stall, `latencyMs=12011`, exit 100 ms later.\n3. Watchdog: `printf 20000 > files/debug/polish-deadline-ms` (hard 22 s, above the watchdog) with the\n   30 s stall still in place. Expect `Polish watchdog fired` at about 15 s, the engine cancel logged, and\n   the fallback published with `WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT`; the engine ends itself as soon as the session\n   unbinds (`destroyed with 1 local request(s) in flight`), before its own 22 s timer. Remove both\n   files. Measured 2026-09-01: watchdog at 15.0 s from the stall, exit 180 ms later.\n4. Cancel: start a dictation with the 40 s fixture, stop it, tap Cancel on the \"Preparing your words\"\n   notification within the transcription window (about 3 s): expect `Cancelled while processing`, no\n   text, no History row, and either the engine's cancel or the transcript dropped by the state check.\n   Driving it: our notification's body and actions are NOT in the `uiautomator dump` (only its timestamp\n   is), so read positions off `screencap`. With ours newest at the top of the shade (1080x2340): chevron\n   at (972,950); expanded, Stop at (302,1097) and Cancel at (778,1097); the processing notification's\n   single Cancel is centred at (540,1145), and (540,1097) hits it. Tapping the body fires the content\n   intent, which STOPS the recording. A longer recording widens the window (84 s of audio gave 2 s of\n   transcription plus polish). Measured 2026-09-01: Stop to Cancel 2.1 s, ASR unbound 140 ms later.\nRestore: both files removed, the mode the phone had before, engine process ended.\n\n## FACT: the-polish-outcome-uat\nThe recipe for #77 and for any change to what the user is told about a failed polish. Stage a real\nprovider rejection without spending: on the AI Polish screen choose Cloud, Gemini, type any non-blank key\n(the screen's Check is a format check), tap Check, tap a model; the key is saved in the Keystore.\nDictate the 11 s fixture from the launcher: expect\n`reason=HTTP_KEY_REJECTED status=400` (the real Gemini 400 body carries `API_KEY_INVALID`),\n`Polish notice shown: KEY_REJECTED`, the toast \"Polish failed. Using raw text.\", a silent notification\n\"AI polish failed\" with the full sentence, and the History card's polish line \"AI polish failed: Gemini\nrejected your API key. Check or replace it in Settings.\" over \"Cleaned up on this phone\". Measured\n2026-09-01. Two traps found the same day: the app had never declared the Internet permission, so every\ncloud request failed in 34 ms as `NETWORK` (fixed in #77); and a toast shows two lines and truncates the\nrest, which is why the reason lives in a notification. Restore: \"Remove saved provider and key\" on the\nscreen, mode back to Off.\n\n## RULE: report-a-skipped-device-test-as-not-run\nInstrumented tests use `assumeTrue` for preconditions such as the PCM fixture, so a missing precondition\nreports SKIPPED. A skipped receipt is not a passed receipt. Say \"not run\", never \"passed\".\n\n## FACT: shizuku-is-not-ours\nShizuku grants shell-level permissions to on-device tooling. EnviousWispr does not depend on it; it matters\nonly for the phone's own Claude Code autonomy. Owner: [phone-bridge.md](phone-bridge.md).\n---\npaths:\n  - \"app/src/**\"\n  - \"llama-android/src/**\"\n  - \"**/build.gradle.kts\"\n  - \"app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml\"\n---\n\n# Architecture Rules\n\nInstructions only. The map — modules, packages, processes, pipeline, sources of truth — is\n[`../knowledge/architecture.md`](../knowledge/architecture.md). The design target is\n[`docs/enviouswispr-android-architecture.md`](../../docs/enviouswispr-android-architecture.md); the outcome\ncontract is [`docs/enviouswispr-android-parity-spec.md`](../../docs/enviouswispr-android-parity-spec.md).\n**Both describe where we are going and name types that do not exist. Grep before citing one.**\n\n## FACT: the-laws\n| Law | Why |\n|---|---|\n| Heart path is sacred. | No optional feature may prevent the user getting their words. |\n| Process boundaries are real boundaries. | `:audio`, `:asr` and `:polish` bound memory and crash blast radius. |\n| Convenience is not justification. | \"Easy to wire here\" is invalid placement. |\n| New shared objects are guilty until proven innocent. | Every coordinator, manager and singleton justifies its existence. |\n| Engine independence lives at the adapter seam. | One session owner, never one per surface. |\n| Structural drift is a bug. | Architecture regression is correctness debt. |\n| Shortcuts must be declared. | Disclose every temporary compromise in the change summary. |\n\n## FACT: heart-and-limbs\n**Heart:** trigger, capture, ASR, text finalization, insertion. It must always complete.\n**Limbs:** deterministic cleanup, vocabulary, local polish, cloud polish, live preview, history.\n\n**The fallback floor is the LAST SUCCESSFUL TEXT, not raw ASR.** Cleanup and vocabulary run before polish\nprecisely so their result survives a polish failure. Only empty output falls through to raw ASR.\n\nA limb hands back the last good value. Never an exception that unwinds the session, never `null` where the\ncaller has no slot for it, and never an empty string as a failure signal — empty is a legitimate\ntranscription of silence and the caller cannot tell them apart.\n\nBefore adding a feature: heart or limb? Owning package? Owning process? Failure mode? Can the heart\ncontinue? Fuzzy answers mean blocked.\n\n## RULE: one-owner-for-the-session\nEvery entry point issues COMMANDS to one session owner. No surface runs its own recording, transcription,\npolish or insertion, and no surface invents its own phase; each renders the owner's state.\n\nWhen the coordinator replaces today's session service, it lands in one change — old code removed, new code\nwired, no shim (`GR-MIGRATION-COMPLETE`).\n\n## RULE: aidl-is-append-only\nReordering, renaming, or changing a parameter list breaks an already-installed app at RUNTIME with no\ncompile error. Append at the end. To change a signature, bump the interface and keep the old one until\nnothing binds it. The separately installed client this protects is the instrumentation APK\n(`app-debug-androidTest.apk`), which binds the non-exported services and is not replaced when the\nproduction APK is, so \"both ends ship in one APK\" is not a reason to delete a transaction.\n\n## RULE: keep-central-types-thin\nA multi-domain owner delegates downward, holds minimal state, exposes a narrow surface, and has a\none-sentence purpose. Block unrelated-domain knowledge, and state plus orchestration plus business rules\nin one place.\n\n**`ui/AppShell.kt` and `ui/DictationSessionService.kt` are the standing extraction targets.** Take the\nsizes rather than citing a count:\n\n```bash\nwc -l app/src/main/java/com/envi/wispr/ui/AppShell.kt app/src/main/java/com/envi/wispr/ui/DictationSessionService.kt\n```\n\nGrowth in either needs a reason and a named extraction target. Add a screen file rather than a section\nto `AppShell.kt` (`TranscriptionScreen.kt`, `PolishScreen.kt`, `SettingsPages.kt`, `ModelCards.kt`,\n`HistoryScreen.kt`, `DictionaryScreen.kt`, `OnboardingScreen.kt` are the precedent). Since #190 the shell\nholds only route state and the exhaustive screen `when`: the top bar, bottom bar, drawer and glyphs are\n`AppNavigation.kt` (with `AppRoutes`, the one reader of the saved route names), the shared rows, chips and\nglyphs are `SettingsComponents.kt`, and the activity hands the shell one `AppActions` holder of ten\ncapability groups built inside `remember(viewModel)`; a new callback joins its group, never the root\nsignature. `ui/AppShellShapeTest` pins all three. The session service's user-facing sentences live in\n`insertion/InsertionOutcomeMessages.kt`.\n\n## RULE: isolate-limbs\nA limb must not root into app-wide, window, or insertion-orchestration state. Every limb has a deadline, a\nfailure path, and an unchanged-text fallback.\n\n**Only one heavy inference process is resident by default.** S1-mini and the Parakeet encoder are each\nseveral hundred megabytes; both resident is not a supported state. Unload before switching engines when\nheadroom is unsafe, and never load a heavy model in the main UI process. Warm-at-connect is the stage 1\ndefault (#72, measured 2026-09-01 on the S26 Ultra only, debug build, so it establishes neither general\nS26, release-build, nor other-device safety: a later warm-up did not reduce peak residency and added 0.8\nto 3.1 s of wait; table in\n`docs/feature-requests/issue-72-2026-09-01-model-residency-decision.md` §11.1.1). The levers that would\nreduce residency are releasing the speech model after transcription (#73) and the NPU polish model (#21).\n\n## RULE: gate-on-capability-not-identity-literal\nFeature gates read a declared capability, never an engine or provider identity literal. `when (provider)`\nis correct only where the behaviour genuinely IS about identity — the privacy disclosure is the legitimate\ncase.\n\n**Where an identity `when` is legitimate it must be EXHAUSTIVE with no `else`.** A new `PolishProvider`\nmust break the build at every disclosure and routing site. An `else` turns that compile error into a\nshipped wrong privacy answer.\n\n## RULE: own-state-locally\nKeep state near its owning domain; never centralise it because many layers read it. The declared sources of\ntruth are in [`../knowledge/architecture.md`](../knowledge/architecture.md); **a second home for any of them\nis a bug.**\n\n## RULE: minimize-visibility\nKotlin defaults to `public`, so the default is wrong. Declare `private`, then `internal`. Only a type\ncrossing a Gradle module boundary needs `public`.\n\n## RULE: protect-audio-asr-stability\nAudio and ASR changes prioritise stability, minimise blast radius, keep rollback clear, and attach measured\nevidence from the physical phone. UI coupling to service internals is a warning sign.\n\n**Never do work on the audio callback thread.** No allocation, no logging, no binder call, no lock another\nthread can hold. Buffer and hand off.\n\n## RULE: no-idle-cost\nAt idle: no timer, no amplitude poll, no accessibility traversal, no binder call, no wake lock, no resident\nmodel. Audio levels are PUSHED from the capture process during a session, not polled by each surface. The\naccessibility service remembers only the last focused editable node identity and ignores our own windows.\n\nA background poll is a battery regression even when it is cheap, because the standard is zero, not small.\n\n## RULE: insertion-fails-safe-never-silently\nOne route, one write (#141): return to the tracked editor and pick exactly one route BEFORE writing. On\nAPI 33+ with an eligible field, commit through the accessibility input connection (no clipboard, no\n\"Copied\" toast); otherwise `ACTION_PASTE`; otherwise copy-only with a visible Paste action. Judge success\nfrom the editor's own text, never the caret. Never `ACTION_SET_TEXT`.\n\n**A stale, missing or unsupported target keeps the transcript on the clipboard and tells the user.** It\nnever inserts into whatever happens to be focused now.\n\n## FACT: there-is-no-sensitive-field-guard-and-that-is-decided\n**Founder decision 2026-08-28: EnviousWispr does not special-case password, payment or OTP fields.** If\nthe user dictates into one, we insert. Three reasons, so no session rebuilds it: Google Play's\nAccessibilityService policy requires disclosure and forbids autonomous operation but is silent on field\ntypes (verified 2026-08-28); the same shape was killed on\nmacOS after a probe showed Secure Input does not block our paste; and as built it refused only the\nharmless insertion step while putting the transcript on the SYSTEM CLIPBOARD and still sending it to\nhistory and cloud polish.\n\nRebuilding it requires new evidence and a guard placed where the exposure is (before cloud polish and\nbefore history), never at the insertion step.\n\n**The code has not caught up:** `paste/PasteAccessibilityService.isSensitive` and\n`InsertionResults.COPY_ONLY_SENSITIVE` still divert to clipboard-only. Removing them is\n[issue #11](https://github.com/Envious-Labs-LLC/EnviousWispr-Android/issues/11), heart path, so it needs\nthe review gate and a hardware run.\n\n## RULE: models-are-pinned-verified-and-app-private\nEvery model descriptor carries a pinned revision and every model file an exact byte count and SHA-256;\n`isAvailable` refuses anything failing those or whose URL omits the pinned revision. Ready only after on-device verification;\nfailed files quarantined, never loaded. Files stay in app-private storage — do not reintroduce a broad\nexternal-storage permission.\n\n## RULE: architecture-definition-of-done\nTriggers: Gradle modules, process assignment, AIDL surface, a new coordinator, state ownership, package\nboundaries, cross-module visibility, or logic moved across layers. Uncertainty blocks work pending Codex\nreview (`GR-ESCALATE-CONSEQUENTIAL`).\n\n- **Placement** — correct package and process; ownership explained in one or two sentences.\n- **Heart** — the user still gets text when every optional feature fails.\n- **Anti-god-object** — no convenience logic in `AppShell.kt` or the session service.\n- **API** — narrowest visibility; no service internals leaked to UI.\n- **Boundaries** — no upward dependency; no UI type reaching a service.\n- **Validation** — unit tests green, plus a hardware run for any heart-path change, with the evidence\n  named. Untested edges stated explicitly.\n- **Debt** — shortcuts disclosed; follow-up extraction named.\n\n## RULE: parity-work-cites-its-contract-id\nName the `PAR-###` row and the evidence that closes it. Parity is the same user OUTCOME, never a literal\nimitation of a macOS mechanism. A row is closed by evidence, not by code existing.\n---\npaths:\n  - \"app/src/test/**\"\n  - \"app/src/androidTest/**\"\n  - \"llama-android/src/**\"\n  - \"accelerator-benchmark/src/**\"\n---\n# Android Testing Patterns\n\n**How to WRITE a test here.** Whether it should EXIST is `testing-philosophy.md`; whether it is HONEST is\n`validation-discipline.md`; how to RUN it is `android-tooling.md`.\n\n## FACT: the-two-source-sets-answer-different-questions\n| Source set | Runs on | Can answer | Cannot answer |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `app/src/test/` | The JVM, no Android framework | Pure logic: cleanup, vocabulary, insertion text planning, manifest validation, prompt building, settings state | Anything touching `Context`, Room, the Keystore, a service, or hardware |\n| `app/src/androidTest/` | The physical S26 Ultra | Room migrations, the Keystore, AIDL services, accessibility insertion, the real microphone, the real models | Nothing about a device we do not own |\n\n## RULE: put-the-case-where-the-fixture-already-is\nThe scarce things in this suite are the rigs that stage a hard state. Before building a new one, check\nwhether one of these already reaches it:\n\n| Rig | Stages |\n|---|---|\n| `PasteTargetActivity` / `ClipboardPasteTargetActivity` | A real focused editable field for insertion tests |\n| `VoicePipelineDeviceTest` | The whole heart on hardware, binding `:asr` and `:polish` |\n| `EnviousWisprDatabaseMigrationTest` | Room schema versions from `app/schemas/` |\n| `SpeakerPlaybackActivity` | Real audio playback into the real microphone |\n\nA test filed by what it is ABOUT rather than by which fixture reaches it lands beside cases that cannot\nstage it, and the next move is a second rig for a state something else already stages.\n\n## RULE: a-device-test-declares-its-precondition-with-assume\n`VoicePipelineDeviceTest` uses `assumeTrue` for its PCM fixture. Follow that shape for every device\nprecondition — models installed, accessibility enabled, a fixture present. **Never let a missing\nprecondition produce a green.**\n\n## RULE: never-sleep-wait-for-the-subject\nNo `Thread.sleep`, no `delay()` as a settle, no polling loop with a retry budget standing in for a signal.\n\n- Coroutines: `runTest` with a `TestDispatcher`, and advance the scheduler.\n- AIDL and callbacks: a `CountDownLatch` awaited with a timeout, counted down BY the callback — the shape\n  `VoicePipelineDeviceTest` already uses. The timeout is a failure bound, not the wait.\n- Compose: `waitUntil` on a semantics condition, never a frame count.\n\n**A budget that exhausts is indistinguishable from the condition it was measuring.** When a wait times\nout, the failure message names what it was waiting for and what it observed instead, so a slow phone and a\nreal bug are distinguishable in one read.\n\n## RULE: assert-the-editor-not-the-clipboard\nClipboard publication is the FALLBACK path. A test that asserts the clipboard holds the text has verified\nthe fallback and said nothing about insertion. Assert the target editor's own field content and its caret,\nwhich is what the paste-target activities exist for.\n\nFor the back-to-back case the assertion is that the SECOND transcript reaches the editor, with the first\none's text still present and not duplicated. A test that dictates once proves nothing about it.\n\n## RULE: build-the-expected-value-with-a-literal\nWhen asserting that a transformation preserves something, write the expected value out by hand. Building\nit by running the same helper the subject runs means both sides get transformed identically and the row\npasses against code that does nothing. `VocabularyCoreTest.transferRoundTripPreservesAdversarialText` is\nthe right shape: hard-coded adversarial input, compared to a hard-coded expectation.\n\n## RULE: adversarial-input-is-a-row-not-a-suite\nOne representative case per input CLASS — empty, whitespace-only, very long, non-Latin script, emoji,\nembedded escapes, RTL, a lone surrogate — at one representative branch, not the Cartesian product.\n`VocabularyCoreTest` carries the vocabulary ones; extend it rather than starting a parallel suite.\n\n## RULE: room-schema-changes-ship-their-migration-test\n`app/schemas/com.envi.wispr.history.EnviousWisprDatabase/` holds the committed schema JSON, and\n`androidTest` includes it as an asset via the `sourceSets` block in `app/build.gradle.kts`. Every version\nbump adds a migration and a test that migrates real rows and asserts the data survived. A migration test\nthat only checks the schema opens has tested the schema, not the user's history.\n\n## RULE: name-the-test-after-the-outcome-it-protects\n`exportRefusesToSilentlyTruncateAnOversizedLibrary` says what breaks for a user. `testExport` does not.\nRead the name back as a promise, then ask what the WEAKEST input satisfying the assertion looks like; if\nthat input would not embarrass the name, the assertion is too loose.\n\n## RULE: declare-the-test-class-in-the-suite-header\nEach suite's KDoc states which of the four classes it protects. Owner: `testing-philosophy.md`\nRULE: every-test-declares-which-of-four-things-it-protects.\n\n## RULE: no-ignore-to-get-a-green\n`@Ignore` on a failing test hides a regression under a passing suite. Fix it, or delete it under\n`testing-philosophy.md` RULE: deleting-a-test-carries-the-burden-of-adding-one, and say which you did.\n---\npaths:\n  - \"app/src/**\"\n  - \"llama-android/src/**\"\n  - \"accelerator-benchmark/src/**\"\n  - \"**/build.gradle.kts\"\n---\n# Testing Philosophy\n\n**Should this test EXIST?** Is it HONEST: `validation-discipline.md`. How to write it:\n`android-testing-patterns.md`. How to run it: `android-tooling.md`.\n\nFounder mandate: test the things that must always work; stop paying for scenarios a real user on a\nsupported phone cannot produce.\n\n## RULE: every-test-declares-which-of-four-things-it-protects\nComplete the sentence **\"when this fails, the user sees ___.\"** If you can finish it, it is a Product\nOutcome test. If you cannot, it is one of the other three and must be NAMED as such — never counted as, or\ncited as, product coverage.\n\n| Class | Protects | Counts as product coverage |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Product Outcome** | Audio captured, text produced, text inserted, a limb degrading to the last successful text | YES |\n| **Drift Guard** | A frozen internal property: Room schema, manifest shape, call-site inventory | NO |\n| **Observability Contract** | Log labels and content-free diagnostics | NO |\n| **Harness Contract** | Our fakes, fixtures, device scaffolding | NO |\n\nDeclare the class in the suite's KDoc; there is no mechanical tag yet, and claiming one exists is wrong.\nAll four are legitimate. The defect this prevents is ARITHMETIC — counting drift guards as user safety.\n\n## RULE: the-heart-crosses-a-real-boundary-at-least-once\nEvery heart-path stage has at least ONE test crossing its REAL boundary. Fakes are correct for the other\nthousand cases and never substitute for the one.\n\n| Stage | Real boundary | Why a fake is insufficient |\n|---|---|---|\n| Capture | A real microphone producing non-zero samples | A dead `AudioRecord` reports \"recording\" and captures silence |\n| Transcription | The shipped model decoding a committed clip | Packaging or ABI breaks while a mock still returns text |\n| Polish | The shipped model on the real runtime | A runtime init failure is invisible to a fake that returns polished text |\n| Insertion | Text landing in a real third-party editor, exactly once | Calling `ACTION_PASTE` proves the call, never arrival |\n\nOnly an instrumented test reaches the last two. A unit test that stubs the AIDL service is a Harness\nContract test, whatever it is named.\n\n## RULE: a-public-product-promise-needs-a-binding-test\nAny claim about speed, capacity, a limit, or privacy gets ONE test that fails when the claim stops being\ntrue. Name the claim and its source in the test.\n\nThe privacy claims are load-bearing here because they bind the Play Data Safety form. A `when` over\n`PolishProvider` gaining a member without a matching disclosure row is the shape that ships a wrong Data\nSafety answer.\n\n**A promise about a SIDE EFFECT is the axis \"speed, capacity, or a limit\" misses, and a UI can hide it.** A\ndeletion claim does not show itself, so it drifts for as long as nobody looks at app-private storage.\nHiding is not deleting.\n\n## RULE: dont-test-what-cannot-happen\nClassify REPRODUCIBLE (a real user on a supported phone produces it; state the input) or HYPOTHETICAL\n(needs a misbehaving dependency, a hostile value, or an unobserved race).\n\n**Write a case for a hypothetical ONLY when the failure would be SILENT** — wrong text inserted, a\ntranscript lost, a limb failing without falling back, a key reaching a log. A hypothetical failing LOUDLY\ngets a recorded known limit.\n\nThe supported platform bounds this absolutely; there is no API 29 scenario and no 32-bit scenario. Devices\nwithout the vendor NPU runtime are a real scenario only once a CPU fallback ships — until then say \"not\nsupported\", not \"untested\".\n\n## RULE: the-rig-decides-where-a-test-lives-not-the-subject\nAsk **which existing fixture already reaches this state**, and put the case there. A test filed by what it\nis ABOUT lands beside cases that cannot stage it, and the next move is a second rig for a state something\nelse already stages. The rigs are named in `android-testing-patterns.md`.\n\n**Two ways a fixture misses, and only the first is fixed by moving.** A fixture that reaches its subject\nand asserts the wrong thing is repaired in place. A fixture whose subject DOES NOT EXIST in that\nconfiguration cannot be repaired at all — editing the assertion turns it into a passing test about nothing.\n\n**A failing new test must name WHAT IT FOUND**, not merely that an expectation failed.\n\n## RULE: do-not-multiply-independent-axes\nTest every BRANCH on one ordinary input, then each special input CLASS at one representative branch. Never\nthe Cartesian product. A row earns its place only by reaching a different production branch or reproducing\na distinct OBSERVED defect.\n\n## RULE: never-guess-when-the-subject-is-finished\nA test learns the subject is done from a signal the SUBJECT fires — never elapsed time, a `delay()`, a\npoll, or the harness going quiet.\n\n**A COUNT THAT EXHAUSTS IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE CONDITION IT WAS MEASURING.** A loop inferring \"the\nstop never arrived\" from a budget running out accuses production code when the harness merely ran out of\nbudget. Do not close one by raising the cap.\n\n**The same missing signal produces the VACUITY direction, which is worse because nothing goes red.** Flake\nand vacuity are one defect wearing two symptoms.\n\n## RULE: a-flaky-suite-earns-no-new-cases-until-its-wait-seam-is-fixed\nThe next change to a flaking suite is the seam fix. Not a rerun, not a longer timeout, not another case.\n**Raising a wait budget is a silent coverage loss unless you name a regression the old value would have\ncaught and the new one would not.** This bites hardest on device tests, where a real timing bug and a slow\nphone look identical.\n\n## RULE: deleting-a-test-carries-the-burden-of-adding-one\nName what it protected, then either why that protection is no longer needed or where it now lives. \"It\nnever caught anything\" is not evidence — a good test never catching anything is the expected case. Never\ndelete or weaken a guard to move a number.\n\n**\"Covered elsewhere\" quantifies over DEFECTS, not over the runs you did.** The claim that licenses a\ndeletion is: is there any defect for which this row is the only red one?\n# Grounding Discipline\n\nHow to find out what is true before acting.\n\n## RULE: lookup-ladder\nStop at the first tier that answers. NAME any Tier 1 or Tier 2 skip in chat; if accidental, stop and use\nthat tier.\n\n**Split the question first.** \"What should EnviousWispr DO here\" is a product question; macOS answers it.\n\"How does this framework work\" is a platform question; macOS cannot. Taking a product question down the\nplatform ladder rebuilds solved behaviour.\n\n| Tier | Source | Use when |\n|---|---|---|\n| 0 | `.claude/knowledge/` and `docs/` | An EnviousWispr Android decision, gotcha, or past investigation. Route via `.claude/knowledge/INDEX.md`. |\n| 1 | The cross-platform catalog, then `catalog_gap` | **Any question about what EnviousWispr does.** Queries in CLAUDE.md. |\n| 2 | The shipping macOS source and its knowledge corpus | The catalog was thin or answered about another mechanism. |\n| 3 | Vendor MCP | Live data or vendor-maintained docs. |\n| 4 | `context7` (`resolve-library-id` → `query-docs`) | AndroidX, Compose, Room, WorkManager, Kotlin, Gradle. Use even when you think you know. One call PER CONCEPT. |\n| 5 | Pinned dependency source (`~/.gradle/caches/modules-2/`, `third_party/llama.cpp/`, the unpacked `.aar`) | Vendor internals and undocumented behaviour. |\n| 6 | The physical phone over ADB | A runtime question source cannot answer. `../knowledge/device-testing.md`. |\n| 7 | WebFetch / WebSearch | Every tier above returned nothing. Cite the URL. |\n| 8 | Ask Saurabh | Product, business, or preference only. Never technical lookups. |\n\n## RULE: a-catalog-hit-does-not-end-the-search\nA hit closes the discovery step only; it never proves the mechanism, the current behaviour, or absence. A\nhit about a NEIGHBOURING mechanism is not an answer: verify the row covers the mechanism under\ninvestigation. The trap is a well-formed answer under a name matching your symptom.\n\n**Grep the PINNED tree.** `third_party/llama.cpp` is a submodule at a fixed commit and GenieX is pinned to\none version; upstream docs describe code we are not running.\n\n## RULE: absence-claims-need-a-capability-grep\nEvery \"we have no X\" or \"no consumers\" claim requires a pasted search for the CAPABILITY's synonyms, never\nfor the name you expect.\n\n- Search every relevant root, including the gitignored `.claude/`, `docs/` and `CLAUDE.md` (`git grep`\n  cannot see them). Justify every excluded root; the root to worry about is one where a DIFFERENT KIND of\n  answer would live (a knowledge file holds RECIPES).\n- Paste every hit uncurated and classify incidental matches.\n- **Closed-world** (an `enum class`, a sealed hierarchy, an AIDL interface, the manifest's `<service>` set):\n  cite the authority `file:line`, paste the enumeration, state expected versus observed counts, account\n  for every member.\n- **Open-world** (external consumers, Play policy, vendor rules): write \"no implementation found in\n  `<sources>`\", never \"X does not exist\".\n- An absence claim expires fast here because Codex writes into the same tree; re-run any sweep before\n  acting on it.\n- \"This needs a decision\" is an absence claim: sweep the PRODUCERS of the value, not only the reader.\n- A capability reached through a Kotlin default argument has no call-site token: make the default fail\n  closed and read the callers off the first run.\n\n## RULE: read-the-fact-not-the-first-n-lines\nIndex a knowledge file with `grep -n \"^## RULE:\\|^## FACT:\"`, then read the matching entry. Before citing\nan entry as CURRENT, read its scope qualifier and date, and grep the same file for a newer entry on the\nsame capability; a rule NARROWED rather than deleted is silent. If two files disagree, fix the DRY defect\nthat session: one owner, one cross-link.\n\n## RULE: grep-the-dependency-before-hand-rolling\nWorkManager already owns unique work, backoff, constraints and observable state. Room owns transactions and\nmigrations. DataStore owns typed consistent reads. Lifecycle owns scope cancellation. Read what the library\nships before designing a manager, retry loop, coalescer or state machine around it. Keep genuinely-ours\npolicy in a thin layer, never a parallel machine.\n\n## RULE: measure-before-composing\nProduce the numbers BEFORE writing the claim, and state the denominator and the source. Never compose a\nquantitative generalisation and measure after a reviewer challenges it.\n\n**A summary invents a claim nobody asked for.** Say what is true of each item, or say what is true of all\nand check that separately.\n\n## RULE: public-claims-need-binding-evidence\nBefore publishing a promise about speed, capacity, a limit, or a SIDE EFFECT, name the evidence that fails\nwhen the promise stops being true. **Ask whether the thing promised is OBSERVABLE** — a latency claim shows\nitself; a deletion or retention claim does not, so it drifts for as long as nobody looks.\n\nThis binds hardest on the Play listing and the privacy disclosure, where a wrong claim is a policy\nviolation, not an error. Owner: `../knowledge/play-store-readiness.md`.\n\n## RULE: never-hand-a-reviewer-an-unchecked-premise\nEvery fact asserted in a Codex or council prompt carries the plan's evidence burden: verify it or label it\n\"not verified\". A CODE COMMENT justifying a design choice carries the same burden.\n\n- **Highest cost: a comment claiming a mechanism ENFORCES something.** Ask what happens if someone adds a\n  member TODAY; if nothing, replace the comment with an exhaustive `when` the compiler owns. A\n  `listOf(...)` is not exhaustive over an enum, nor is a `when` with an `else`.\n- **A claim about what your OWN change makes true** has no oracle but the diff you are still writing.\n  Carry the property in control flow, not in a paragraph.\n- Also check: every claim a user-visible surface exists; every positional claim, rechecked after any\n  move; every log line asserting a mechanism the call site did not observe; every comment declaring a\n  question CLOSED, which must state what was measured and what would reopen it.\n- Read a SHARED comment block per SITE; when review names one instance, grep the SENTENCE.\n- A claim you can VERIFY mechanically is never verified by reading: grep every backticked identifier\n  against the working tree, including uncommitted lines.\n- Attribute to the RUN or the `file:line`, never to a person or session; refuse an attribution aimed at\n  you for a measurement you did not produce.\n- A correction carries the same burden in both directions: resolve it to a `file:line` and read that line.\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Keystore secret store, validation |\n| `privacy/` | The provider disclosure table |\n| `settings/` | DataStore preferences, custom words store |\n| `shortcuts/` | Quick Settings tile, notification controller, overlay state |\n| `ui/` | Compose shell (`AppShell.kt`: route state and the screen `when`; `AppNavigation.kt`: chrome, drawer and `AppRoutes`; `SettingsComponents.kt`: shared rows, chips, glyphs; `AppActions.kt`: the ten action groups the activity hands the shell, #190), one file per screen, view model, settings activity, recorder activity, the session owner (`DictationSessionCoordinator.kt`, the take's state machine and every decision, behind the seams `SessionHost`, `RecorderSurface`, `InsertionGateway`, `SessionLog`, `PipelineController` over `PipelineLinks.kt`, `SessionPreferencesSource`, `PolishTimeout`; #186) and its Android shell `DictationSessionService.kt` |\n| `debug/` | Content-free logging |\n| `model/` | Model lifecycle and unload policy |\n| `vad/` | `SilenceVadService`, Silero VAD through sherpa-onnx, the stop-on-silence detector — process `:vad` |\n| `about/` | Release notes |\n\nThere is no `ime/` package and none may be added (`../rules/code-gotchas.md` RULE: enviouswispr-is-not-a-keyboard).\n\n## FACT: processes-and-their-contract\n`app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` is the authority.\n\n- **main** — Compose UI, Room, DataStore, session ownership. It owns the polish POLICY: the session owner\n  latches one snapshot per session and sends it with every request (#69).\n- **`:audio`** — `AudioCaptureService`.\n- **`:asr`** — `AsrService`.\n- **`:vad`** — `SilenceVadService`, alone because sherpa calls `exit(-1)` on a contract violation.\n- **`:polish`** — `PolishService`, so S1's memory is isolated from ASR's; also where cloud polish calls\n  run. It holds no settings: `polish-engines.md` FACT: the-engine-holds-no-settings.\n\nThey talk over six AIDL interfaces and two parcelables in `app/src/main/aidl/`. AIDL is append-only — owner:\n`../rules/architecture-rules.md` RULE: aidl-is-append-only.\n\n## FACT: entry-points\nSix surfaces reach one session owner (`ui.DictationSessionService`, whose every command goes to its\n`DictationSessionCoordinator`, #186); none runs its own pipeline.\n\n| Surface | Mechanism |\n|---|---|\n| The lips bubble (primary, #135, on `main` via #140) | `paste.RecordingAccessibilityOverlay`'s idle shape, hosted by `paste.PasteAccessibilityService`; a tap or hold sends `ACTION_START` straight to the owner with a `shortcuts.BubbleRequests` token, falling back to `ui.VoiceInputActivity` only when the direct start is refused |\n| Samsung side button, double press | Samsung \"Open app\" mapped to `ui.VoiceInputActivity` via `android.intent.action.ASSIST` |\n| Floating recorder | `ui.VoiceInputActivity` — `singleTop`, `noHistory`, `excludeFromRecents`, its own task affinity; transparency comes from its theme |\n| Quick Settings tile | `shortcuts.DictationTileService`, an ACTIVE tile |\n| Notification | `shortcuts.DictationNotificationController` |\n| The app | `ui.SettingsActivity`, the launcher activity hosting the Compose shell |\n\n## FACT: the-text-pipeline\nEach stage returns text plus an outcome. A stage may enrich text; it may never erase the last valid result.\n\n1. ASR produces raw text and an observed language.\n2. Deterministic cleanup applies filler, number and punctuation rules.\n3. Vocabulary correction applies exact terms, aliases, case rules and priority.\n4. Optional polish runs, local or cloud, under the policy snapshot the session carries; the answer is one\n   `PolishOutcome` per request, with a `PolishReason` from a closed set.\n5. Output safety rejects blank, truncated, duplicated or meaning-shifted results and falls back.\n6. Insertion planning handles capitalisation, spacing, seam de-duplication and the replacement range.\n7. Accessibility returns to the tracked editor and picks ONE route before writing: on API 33+ with an\n   eligible field it commits through the accessibility input connection (no clipboard, no \"Copied\"\n   toast); otherwise `ACTION_PASTE`; otherwise copy-only with a visible Paste action. It writes once,\n   judges success from the editor's text, never the caret, and never uses `ACTION_SET_TEXT` (#141).\n\n**Cleanup and vocabulary run BEFORE polish on purpose**, so their result survives a polish failure.\n\n## FACT: sources-of-truth\nA second home for any of these is a bug.\n\n| Data | Owner |\n|---|---|\n| Settings and onboarding progress | DataStore, `settings/AppPreferences.kt` |\n| Transcript history and recovery | Room, `history/EnviousWisprDatabase.kt`, schema in `app/schemas/` |\n| Custom terms | Room, `vocabulary/CustomTermDao.kt` |\n| Provider secrets | Android Keystore, `providers/AndroidKeystoreSecretStore.kt` |\n| Model catalog | `models/ModelManifest.kt`, compiled in |\n| Model install state | Verified app-private files plus stored metadata |\n| Editor context | Ephemeral accessibility node identity, never persisted as content |\n| Auto-paste permission | Android's `ENABLED_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES`, read only in `ui/AppViewModel.readAppReadiness` |\n| Auto-paste binding liveness | `paste/PasteAccessibilityService.isBound`, written only by `publishBinding` on connect and unbind |\n\nThe two auto-paste rows answer different questions and both are needed: the setting string still names a\nservice that has CRASHED. Code owners: `models/ModelManifest.kt`,\n`models/ModelDelivery.kt`, `models/ModelDeliveryWorker.kt`, `models/ModelStorage.kt`,\n`model/ModelLifecyclePolicy.kt`.\n\n## FACT: the-manifest-is-compiled-in-and-refuses-on-five-axes\n`ModelDescriptor.isAvailable` returns true only when the id is a safe file name, the file list is\nnon-empty, and EVERY file has a safe name, a positive expected byte count, a well-formed SHA-256, a\nvalidated source URL, and a URL containing `/resolve/<pinnedRevision>/`.\n\nThat last clause is what stops a manifest silently drifting to a branch head: a URL missing\n`/resolve/<pinnedRevision>/` makes `isAvailable` false. It is a runtime computed property, so nothing\nfails at compile time — a manifest edit needs its test.\n\n## FACT: what-ships-today\n| Model | Engine | Files | Licence |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `parakeet` | `sherpa-onnx` | `encoder.int8.onnx` 652,184,281 B · `decoder.int8.onnx` 11,845,275 B · `joiner.int8.onnx` 6,355,277 B · `tokens.txt` 93,939 B | CC-BY-4.0, NVIDIA |\n| `s1-mini` | `llama.cpp` | `s1-mini-q4_k_m.gguf` 484,219,808 B | Apache 2.0, Superwhisper |\n\nBoth list `https://models.enviouslabs.co/<prefix>/<revision>/<file>` first (our R2 bucket, shared with\nmacOS and Windows, prefixes `s1/` and `parakeet-onnx/`) and Hugging Face at the pinned revision as the\nfallback (PR #169, #168; all five files live on our host since 2026-09-17, uploaded with a mint-use-revoke\nbucket token per `~/.claude/knowledge/infra/cloudflare.md`; emulator proved both orders that day). Hugging Face: Parakeet is\n`csukuangfj/sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8` at `2bda32ec…`; S1 is\n`superwhisper/s1-mini-GGUF` at `34add00a…`.\n\n**The v2 to v3 bump (2026-09-02, #36) is the worked example of RULE: a-model-version-bump-is-a-content-change.**\nSame four file names, same licence, same engine, so `AsrService` needed no wiring change; what moved was the\nrepo, the revision, four byte counts, four hashes, the assertion in `ModelManifestTest`, and the four\nTranscription strings that promised English. **Every installed copy went unverified the moment the build\nlanded**, because the receipt embeds the revision and every size and hash, so the phone showed Update\navailable and could not dictate until the new files were admitted.\n\n**The NPU-optimised `s1-mini-q4_0.gguf` is NOT in the manifest.** It is a development override only. See\n[polish-engines.md](polish-engines.md).\n\n## RULE: downloads-are-unique-work-that-verifies-before-admitting\nDownloads run as WorkManager unique work keyed by model id, write to a partial file, resume through HTTP\nranges where the host allows it, then validate byte count and SHA-256 and atomically admit the model.\nFailed files are quarantined and never loaded. A model is Ready only after on-device verification.\n\n**Claim the destination atomically; never check for existence and then rename.** A single-threaded test\ncannot tell the two apart. Owner: [`../rules/validation-discipline.md`](../rules/validation-discipline.md)\nRULE: a-single-threaded-test-cannot-distinguish-atomic-from-check-then-act.\n\n## PROCEDURE: place-a-model-by-hand\nRun 2026-08-31 to restore the S26 after a `connectedAndroidTest` uninstall. Every file landed with the\nmanifest's exact byte count and SHA-256, verified ON the phone afterwards.\n\n`ModelStorage.root` is `noBackupFilesDir/models`, so the destination is\n`no_backup/models/<model id>/<file name>` inside app-private storage. `adb push` cannot write there; push\nto `/data/local/tmp` and copy in as the app.\n\n```bash\nADB=~/Android/sdk/platform-tools/adb; D=<serial>\n# 1. Fetch at the PINNED revision. The ids, byte counts and hashes are in models/ModelManifest.kt.\ncurl -fsSL -o encoder.int8.onnx \\\n  \"https://huggingface.co/csukuangfj/sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8/resolve/2bda32ec70b097a55adaa07d9a7173915b43cc78/encoder.int8.onnx?download=true\"\n# 2. Make the directories as the app.\n$ADB -s $D shell 'run-as com.envi.wispr mkdir -p no_backup/models/parakeet no_backup/models/s1-mini'\n# 3. Per file: push, make it readable, copy in as the app, remove the staging copy.\n$ADB -s $D push encoder.int8.onnx /data/local/tmp/encoder.int8.onnx\n$ADB -s $D shell 'chmod 666 /data/local/tmp/encoder.int8.onnx'\n$ADB -s $D shell 'run-as com.envi.wispr cp /data/local/tmp/encoder.int8.onnx no_backup/models/parakeet/encoder.int8.onnx; echo RC=$?'\n$ADB -s $D shell 'rm -f /data/local/tmp/encoder.int8.onnx'\n# 4. THE RECEIPT, without which the files are invisible. See below.\n$ADB -s $D push receipt-parakeet.txt /data/local/tmp/r.txt\n$ADB -s $D shell 'chmod 666 /data/local/tmp/r.txt'\n$ADB -s $D shell 'run-as com.envi.wispr cp /data/local/tmp/r.txt no_backup/models/parakeet/.verified-receipt'\n$ADB -s $D shell 'rm -f /data/local/tmp/r.txt'\n# 5. Verify ON the phone. A matching byte count is not a matching file.\n$ADB -s $D shell \"run-as com.envi.wispr sh -c 'sha256sum no_backup/models/parakeet/* no_backup/models/s1-mini/*'\"\n```\n\n**PLACING THE FILES IS NOT ENOUGH AND THE FAILURE IS SILENT.** `ModelDeliveryStore.isVerified` is what\n`ModelStorage.isReady` answers with, and `AsrService.initRecognizer` refuses without it. It requires a\n`.verified-receipt` in the model directory whose content equals `ModelDeliveryStore.receiptText`, AND that\nthe directory hold EXACTLY the manifest's files plus that receipt — one extra file fails it. With the five\nfiles correct to the byte and the receipt absent, the app said `asr model not loaded` and the Transcription\npage showed the engine as not ready (measured 2026-08-31).\n\nThe receipt is the pinned revision, then one line per file in MANIFEST ORDER, `name=bytes:sha256`, UTF-8,\nno trailing newline. **Generate it from `ModelManifest.kt` rather than typing it** — every value in it is\nalso checked, so a typo reproduces the same silent failure:\n\n```bash\npython3 - <<'GEN'\nimport re, pathlib\nsrc = pathlib.Path(\"app/src/main/java/com/envi/wispr/models/ModelManifest.kt\").read_text()\nrevs = dict(re.findall(r'private const val (\\w+Revision) = \"([0-9a-f]+)\"', src))\nfor var, revkey in ((\"parakeet\", \"parakeetRevision\"), (\"s1\", \"s1Revision\")):\n    block = re.search(r'val %s = ModelDescriptor\\((.*?)\\n    \\)\\)' % var, src, re.S).group(1)\n    model_id = re.match(r'\"([^\"]+)\"', block.strip()).group(1)\n    files = re.findall(r'ModelFile\\(\"([^\"]+)\",\\s*(\\d+),\\s*\"([0-9a-f]{64})\"', block)\n    text = revs[revkey] + \"\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(f\"{n}={b}:{h}\" for n, b, h in files)\n    pathlib.Path(f\"receipt-{model_id}.txt\").write_bytes(text.encode())\n    print(model_id, len(files), \"files\")\nGEN\n```\n\nBoth models read `Ready` on the Transcription and AI Polish pages once their receipt is in place.\n\n**`run-as` takes a command, not a shell, so a glob in it does not expand** — it reports\n`No such file or directory` for the literal `*` and reads as a missing model. Wrap globbing work in\n`sh -c '...'`, as step 4 does.\n\nThe whole restore is 1.1 GB and about ten minutes on a good connection. Permissions and the accessibility\nservice are a separate restore, owned by\n[device-testing.md](device-testing.md) RULE: connectedAndroidTest-UNINSTALLS-the-app-so-never-point-it-at-the-daily-phone.\n\n## FACT: storage\nModel files live in app-private storage and are never backed up, which is correct: they are large,\nre-downloadable and hash-verified. The prototype's broad external-storage permission was removed; there is\nno model-delivery reason to reintroduce it.\n\n## FACT: the-ui-states\n`models/ModelDeliveryUi.kt` owns the mapping from WorkManager and control state to what the user sees, and\n`ModelDeliveryUiTest` binds it. The labels it can produce, read from `modelUiState` on 2026-08-28:\nQueued, Downloading, Verifying, Paused, Checking, Ready, Cancelled, Failed, Update available, Update\nfailed, Repair needed, Missing. The offered actions are `ModelUiAction`: DOWNLOAD, PAUSE, RESUME, RETRY,\nREPAIR, REMOVE, UPDATE, CANCEL, NONE.\n\n**Ready is gated on `verifiedReady`, not on the download succeeding.** A `SUCCEEDED` work state without\nverification shows Checking, and a `FAILED` work state with a previously verified model still shows Ready.\nThat asymmetry is deliberate: the file on disk is the authority, not the job.\n\nThe underlying enums are `DownloadState` (DOWNLOADING, PAUSED, VERIFYING, READY, FAILED, CANCELLED,\nREPAIR_NEEDED) and `ModelDeliveryControlState` (ACTIVE, PAUSED, CANCELLED) in `models/ModelDelivery.kt`.\nDo not take the state list from the design document; it does not match.\n\n**Every size the user reads is DECIMAL, and that is a correctness fact, not a preference.** `ui/ModelCards.kt`\n`formatModelBytes` divides by 1000 because Android's `Formatter.formatFileSize`, the Play listing and the\nfree-space figure all do; a binary divisor under an `MB` label understated every size this app displayed by\nfive percent until #89. `PolishLadderTest.sizesAreInTheDecimalUnitsTheRestOfThePhoneUses` pins the\nconvention at each boundary, so restoring 1024 goes red rather than shipping. It formats in the default\nlocale on purpose, which is why no test asserts an English decimal point.\n\n## FACT: licensing-is-covered-by-two-files-and-one-generator\n`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` at the repository root covers every Maven dependency on the release runtime\nclasspath plus sherpa-onnx, ONNX Runtime and llama.cpp, which have no Maven coordinate. It is GENERATED by\n`scripts/generate-notices.py`, which reads each licence from the publisher's own POM and FAILS CLOSED on a\ndependency it cannot obtain one for; never hand-edit it. `app/src/main/assets/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` is\nthe copy a user reads inside the app (`ui/SettingsActivity.kt`) and owns the MODELS, the bundled font, the\nvoice activity detector and the provider icons.\n\n**Nothing linked either file to what it described, and both went stale (#15, 2026-09-06):** the asset named\nan S1-mini revision the app had abandoned and called llama.cpp Apache-2.0 when llama.cpp's own LICENSE says\nMIT. `ThirdPartyNoticesTest` now binds every claim to its source, so drift goes red instead of shipping.\n\nProduction hosting shipped 2026-09-17 (#169); the manifest stays in the app at a pinned revision, so a model\nbump is an app release (RULE: a-model-version-bump-is-a-content-change). Launch owner:\n[play-store-readiness.md](play-store-readiness.md).\n\n## RULE: a-model-version-bump-is-a-content-change\nChanging a pinned revision, file name, size or quantisation sweeps in-app strings, the Play listing, and\nany outbound link naming the old version, in the same change. Owner:\n[`../rules/content-brand.md`](../rules/content-brand.md)\nRULE: a-multi-home-claim-traces-to-one-orphaned-change.\n     730 .claude/knowledge/device-testing.md\n# Device Testing\n\nThe phone is the only instrument that can answer most questions about this app. **Commands, ADB traps and\nGradle traps live in [`../rules/android-tooling.md`](../rules/android-tooling.md)** — this file owns the\ndevice itself and what to test on it.\n\n## FACT: the-device\n| Property | Value |\n|---|---|\n| Model | Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, `SM-S948U1`, board `canoe`, SoC SM8850 |\n| OS | Android 16, SDK 36 |\n| Accelerators | Adreno 840 GPU, Hexagon HTP NPU |\n| ADB over Tailscale | `100.94.206.47:5555` |\n| SSH into Termux | `ssh -p 8022 u0_a517@100.94.206.47` |\n\nVerified 2026-08-28. It is the founder's daily driver, not a lab device: restore any setting a session\nchanges — screen timeout, stay-awake, developer options, an accessibility service enabled for a test.\n\n## RULE: recover-the-connection-before-diagnosing-anything-else\n**Check Tailscale on the Mac first.** `adb connect` AND `ssh -p 8022` timing out together points at this\nend: `/Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale status` (`Tailscale is stopped` is the tell),\nthen `/Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale up` and `~/Android/sdk/platform-tools/adb connect 100.94.206.47:5555`.\n\nWhen SSH works and ADB does not, three facts decide whether ADB is possible, in this order:\n\n| Question | How to answer it | If no |\n|---|---|---|\n| Is the phone on WiFi? | `ssh … 'ifconfig \\| grep -A1 wlan0'` | Wireless debugging needs WiFi; on cellular there is no ADB route, whatever the toggle says. |\n| Is wireless debugging on? | `ssh … 'nmap -sT -p 30000-49000 localhost -T5 --open'`, then `adb connect localhost:<port>` on each | An open port that refuses `adb connect` is not adbd. Only the founder can flip that switch. |\n| Is the port normalised? | `adb connect 100.94.206.47:5555` from the Mac | After a reboot the port is random again: `adb connect localhost:<port> && adb tcpip 5555 && adb connect localhost:5555`. |\n\n`getprop init.svc.adbd` and `sys.usb.config` read as if they answer this and do not.\n\n`android-bridge/adb-recover.sh` automates the port loop and must run ON THE PHONE\n(`ssh -p 8022 u0_a517@100.94.206.47 'bash ~/android-bridge/adb-recover.sh'`); on the Mac it fails on a\nmissing log path and a WiFi check. If it fails, SSH in, read the port under Settings, Developer options,\nWireless debugging, and run the port loop by hand. Its pidfile guard is not self-healing: if it answers \"Another instance\nrunning\" and exits 0, read `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` before killing, then remove\n`~/android-bridge/adb-recover.pid`.\n\n## RULE: a-watcher-for-the-phone-names-the-phone\n`adb devices | grep -qE \"device$\"` asks \"is A device attached\", and an emulator answers yes. Match the\nserial: `adb devices | grep -qE \"^100\\.94\\.206\\.47:5555[[:space:]]+device$\"`, with a control that the\npattern does NOT match while only the emulator is up.\n\n## RULE: connectedAndroidTest-UNINSTALLS-the-app-so-never-point-it-at-the-daily-phone\n`./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest` installs both APKs, runs, and UNINSTALLS them on the way out,\ntaking app-private storage with it: both models, the history, the custom words, every hand-granted\npermission and the saved settings, so ONBOARDING RETURNS. `scripts/hooks/command-safety.py` denies any\nGradle task named `connected*` and prints the `am instrument` form; an `ANDROID_SERIAL=emulator-*` target\nstill runs.\n\nThe symptom after the fact is `run-as: unknown package`, `pm path` printing nothing, or `am start`\nanswering `Activity class ... does not exist`. Check `pm path com.envi.wispr` FIRST. Restoring is a chore\n(twenty minutes, 1.1 GB):\n\n```bash\n$ADB -s $D install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk\n$ADB -s $D shell 'pm grant com.envi.wispr android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO'\n$ADB -s $D shell 'pm grant com.envi.wispr android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS'\n# READ the setting first and APPEND: it is a colon-separated list and this phone carries another\n# accessibility app; overwriting it turned that one off.\n$ADB -s $D shell settings get secure enabled_accessibility_services\n$ADB -s $D shell settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services \"<existing>:com.envi.wispr/com.envi.wispr.paste.PasteAccessibilityService\"\n$ADB -s $D shell settings put secure accessibility_enabled 1\n```\n\nPass that value as a tool argument, never inside a nested `adb shell '...'` string (quoted inside, it\nstored `null` and disabled every accessibility service on the phone). Then hand-place the models per\n[model-delivery.md](model-delivery.md) PROCEDURE: place-a-model-by-hand. All four steps proven\n2026-08-31. Prefer a manual ADB run for a single question; reach for `connectedAndroidTest` only when the\nrig is genuinely the subject, on the emulator.\n\n**`am instrument` is not safe by itself: READ THE SUITE'S `@Before` FIRST.** `AndroidKeystoreSecretStoreTest.setUp`\nDELETES `no_backup/provider-secrets.v1` unconditionally and `ProviderConfigurationRepositoryTest.setUp`\nclears the real provider preferences, so either class on the founder's phone destroys his hand-entered\nkeys. Storage and Keystore suites ask nothing of the microphone, NPU, side button or a real editor: run\nthem on `emulator-5554`.\n\n## RULE: drive-the-instrumented-tests-with-am-instrument-not-gradle\n`am instrument` does not uninstall, so it is the way to run a device test against the founder's phone:\n\n```bash\nADB=~/Android/sdk/platform-tools/adb\nD=100.94.206.47:5555\n./gradlew :app:assembleDebug :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest\n$ADB -s $D install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk\n$ADB -s $D install -r -t app/build/outputs/apk/androidTest/debug/app-debug-androidTest.apk   # -t: test-only\n$ADB -s $D shell 'am instrument -w -e class com.envi.wispr.VoicePipelineDeviceTest#<method> \\\n    com.envi.wispr.test/androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner'\n```\n\n- **Re-enable accessibility after EVERY `install -r`** (it unbinds the service and clears\n  `enabled_accessibility_services`); set it back, wait a few seconds, never in the same breath as the install.\n- **Generate the spoken audio with Azure Speech** (`~/.claude/knowledge/ai/cloud-llm-credits.md`, voice\n  `en-US-AvaNeural`, `X-Microsoft-OutputFormat: raw-16khz-16bit-mono-pcm` is exactly the headerless\n  fixture format). Write it to BOTH `com.envi.wispr` and `com.envi.wispr.test` under `cache/enviouswispr-uat.pcm`.\n- **`VoicePipelineDeviceTest` REPORTS THE POLISHED TEXT, NOT THE TRANSCRIPT** (`polishedText` is ASR,\n  cleanup, then S1-mini). To measure a stage, bind `:asr` directly in a throwaway probe and fail an\n  assertion carrying `RAW=[...] CLEANED=[...]` (the fixture is our own TTS, so the content rule is not in\n  play); delete the probe afterwards.\n- **Parakeet v3 does its own number and currency formatting** (`$37,200`, `64 gigabytes`); never\n  attribute a formatted number to our code without the raw line.\n- **Known stale assertion:** `launcherRecordsPhonePlaybackAndReachesClipboardStep` requires `(NPU)` in\n  the polish log; this phone reports `(GPU)`, so the row goes red after a dictation that worked.\n\n## FACT: the-ASSIST-action-opens-a-CHOOSER-on-this-phone\n`am start -a android.intent.action.ASSIST` does NOT start the recorder on the S26. It shows Android's\n\"Complete action using\" chooser, because more than one app answers the action and no default is set.\nFounder observed it 2026-08-30 with the dialog on his screen. Launch the component instead:\n\n```bash\n$ADB shell 'am start -n com.envi.wispr/.ui.VoiceInputActivity'\n```\n\nA missing microphone or notification permission sends that activity straight to Settings and no session\nstarts, which reads exactly like the launch failing. Check `dumpsys package com.envi.wispr | grep granted`\nbefore diagnosing anything else.\n\n## FACT: uiautomator-dump-crashes-on-this-phone-INTERMITTENTLY\n`adb shell uiautomator dump` failed on this Android 16 / One UI build on 2026-09-01 with `RC=137` and no XML, logcat\npointing at `UiAutomationShellWrapper.connect()`, with or without any accessibility service bound (so not a\nservice conflict). The same day a dozen-plus calls succeeded, so it CAN fail, not DOES fail: `tree()`\nretries, and after a second 137 answers `Blocked` naming `shot()`, `overlay()` and `last_take()` as the\neyes that still work (RULE: no-appium-and-no-tap-by-position).\n\n## RULE: drive-the-phone-with-wispr-eyes\n`scripts/uat/wispr_eyes.py` is the default way to see and drive the app; the one document for it is\n`../skills/wispr-eyes/SKILL.md`, its own tests `python3 scripts/uat/test_wispr_eyes.py`. Recording from\nit is OFF for the PHYSICAL phone (`RECORDING_IS_OFF`, scoped by `_recording_is_off()` since #177; the\nemulator records); delete that constant only on a review round whose verdict says the take-with-no-debt\nCLASS is closed. Since #177 it is the only door: raw driving commands are refused by\n`scripts/hooks/command-safety.py` (`../rules/tools-and-apps.md` RULE:\ndrive-the-phone-through-wispr-eyes-before-any-raw-adb). Redirect a long run through `python3 -u`, or a backgrounded\n`scan()` writes an empty file for minutes. **After `adb install -r`, force-stop through `stop_app()`, never raw\n`am force-stop`:** a raw force-stop clears the accessibility baseline, `enable_auto_paste()` then journals that\ncleared state as the debt, and `dictate_emulator()` starts with `restore()`, which pays the debt back and reports\nauto-paste off (2026-09-20). `stop_app()` journals the on state first and settles its own debt.\n\n```bash\npython3 scripts/uat/wispr_eyes.py look        # what is on screen\npython3 scripts/uat/wispr_eyes.py scan        # every screen, every switch\npython3 scripts/uat/wispr_eyes.py restore     # put the phone back\npython3 -c \"import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts/uat'); from wispr_eyes import *; print(switches())\"\n```\n\n**Four eyes, and two see the recorder** (measured 2026-09-06 and 2026-09-20, service bound, take running):\n\n| Eye | Sees the app's pages | Sees the floating recorder | Cost |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| the FAST eye: the app's own accessibility service through `DebugDumpReceiver` (`tree()` on a DEBUG build with the service bound; #181) | YES, every window: app, keyboard, status bar, our bubble | YES: `Recording controls`, the clock, Cancel, Stop, as nodes | 0.1 s |\n| the SLOW eye: `uiautomator dump` (`tree()` on a release build or an unbound service) | YES | NO, zero nodes while the pill was on screen | 1.9 s, all of it process start |\n| `screencap` (`shot()`) | YES, as pixels | NO, the home screen with no pill | ~1 s |\n| `dumpsys window windows` (`overlay()`) | geometry only | YES: `EnviousWispr recording controls`, `shown`, `HAS_DRAWN`, `isOnScreen`, `isVisible` reported separately | 0.1 s |\n\nThe fast eye refreshes every node from the live view before reading it: the service's node cache\nreported a switch's OLD state for 1.5 s after a tap (2026-09-20). It reads mid-animation, so anything\nthat turns a reading into a coordinate reads through `_stable_tree()` (two identical reads 0.12 s\napart). Only the shell can ask it (`android.permission.DUMP`); a second debuggable package gets nothing.\n\nAsk the tree about a PAGE, `overlay()` about the RECORDER, and the LOG (`recording()` reads\n`recording_start` against `recording_stop` from `AudioCapture`) about the take. Never tap the pill by a\ncoordinate: `stop_dictation()` / `cancel_dictation()` use `VoiceInputActivity`'s exported `stop` and\n`cancel` extras. `dumpsys notification` keeps our entry after the take ends and is not a witness. A\nscreenshot cannot answer anything about the recorder, including its level meter: the region belongs to\nthe app behind the pill. Whether the meter responds is a question for a screen RECORDING.\n\n## FACT: force-stopping-the-app-CLEARS-the-accessibility-permission\nMeasured 2026-09-06: a force-stop CLEARS `Settings.Secure.enabled_accessibility_services` (`setting=null`\nafterwards), so the user's grant is erased and nothing restores it; every dictation then lands on the\nclipboard. A force-stop reaches real users (app info, a task killer, Samsung's \"put unused apps to sleep\");\nissue #131 owns the product side. Repair, and read `bound()` back rather than the setting string:\n\n```bash\n$ADB shell settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services com.envi.wispr/com.envi.wispr.paste.PasteAccessibilityService\n$ADB shell settings put secure accessibility_enabled 1\n```\n\n`wispr_eyes.stop_app()` repairs after its own force-stops; `enable_auto_paste()` is the repair alone.\n\n## FACT: scrolling-UP-from-near-the-top-pulls-down-the-notification-shade\nA drag that starts in the top strip opens the notification shade, and every later step then reports\n`EnviousWispr is not on screen; showing com.android.systemui`. Start any downward drag below the top sixth\nof the screen (`wispr_eyes.scroll` clamps it); `cmd statusbar collapse` closes a shade and is allowed where\na swipe at a keyguard is not.\n\n## RULE: choose-a-control-by-ANCESTRY-never-by-which-box-surrounds-it\nCompose puts a row's words and its behaviour on different nodes: `SettingsToggleRow` writes its title into\na `TextView` and its state onto the `toggleable` Row that CONTAINS it. Find the words, then walk UP THE\nPARSED TREE (`wispr_eyes.tree()` records each node's `parent`; `_holder` walks it), never \"the smallest\nclickable box whose bounds enclose the label\", because an overlapping control gives the wrong answer and\nthis harness presses buttons that delete a 484 MB model. A flat test fixture cannot catch this; write\nfixtures nested the way the phone reports them.\n\n## RULE: a-change-to-the-phone-must-outlive-the-command-that-made-it\n`wispr_eyes` runs one process per errand, so the \"put it back\" book is a FILE,\n`~/.cache/wispr-eyes/restore.json`, keyed by device serial, written BEFORE the change and cleared only\nafter the restore was read back. A running take is a change in that book, written before the start intent\nand settled after the microphone closes, so any later session's `restore()` ends it.\n\n```bash\ncat ~/.cache/wispr-eyes/restore.json\npython3 -c \"import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/uat'); from wispr_eyes import *; print(restore())\"\n```\n\n## RULE: no-appium-and-no-tap-by-position\nAppium left this project on 2026-09-20 (#177): a UiAutomator2 session holds `UiAutomation`, which unbinds\nthe accessibility service that draws the recorder and inserts text, so every dictation under it hands off\n`SERVICE_NOT_RUNNING`. The harness's eyes replace it (`look()`, `find()`, `overlay()`, `shot()`), and when\n`uiautomator dump` dies twice with 137 the answer is `Blocked` naming those, never a second reader.\n\n**Never tap a control by position.** A clickable ancestor carries no `text`; the label is in a child. A\nsession that inferred \"Refresh\" from position deleted the founder's OpenAI key. **Never press Remove on\nhis phone unless removing is the thing under test** (founder 2026-09-02); a key is not dev state.\nRestoring one is possible from GCP (`~/.claude/bin/get-key launch openai-api-key K -- ...`), but the\nLadder then auto-saves and switches polish to that provider, so the repair changes his settings too.\n`tap('label')` resolves by words; the Bash hook refuses a raw `input tap`.\n\n## FACT: samsung-keyboard-can-float-a-clipboard-suggestion-over-an-inline-button\nThe Samsung keyboard can draw a floating clipboard-suggestion chip above a focused field when the\nclipboard holds content resembling what is typed (seen with a password-type field, #62, 2026-09-01). It\nrenders in the IME layer ABOVE the app and intercepts taps meant for an in-field control such as this\napp's \"Check\". Dismiss it (tap its ✕) or avoid copying test values to the clipboard. Separately, a raw\n`input tap` within about 50 px of the right edge can trigger an OS gesture instead; keep synthetic taps\naway from the outer edge margin, and take bounds from a page source, never from screenshot pixels.\n\n## RULE: one-phone-serialises-every-session\nThere is exactly one device and Codex drives it too. Before a device run, check whether something else is\non it — `dumpsys package com.envi.wispr | grep lastUpdateTime` tells you whether a different build was just\ninstalled. Two sessions installing different builds onto one phone produce results that belong to neither.\n\n## FACT: insertion-is-IMPOSSIBLE-on-a-locked-phone-and-here-is-the-proof\nWhile the phone is secure-locked the accessibility service sees exactly one window, the keyguard, and no\napplication window (measured 2026-09-03: `dumpsys accessibility` shows `type=TYPE_SYSTEM` only and zero\n`envi.wispr.test` windows with the service BOUND and `PasteTargetActivity` top-resumed). Capture, the\ndetector, auto-stop, transcription and polish all run locked, and a fixture with `android:showWhenLocked`\nplays audio into the microphone; only the last hop is unreachable. **Read the bound count before believing\nany window count**: an unbound service also reports zero windows. `dumpsys accessibility | grep -c \"Bound\nservices:{Service\\[label=EnviousWispr\"` first; a bare re-`put` of the same setting string does NOT rebind.\n\n## FACT: a-locked-screen-is-a-real-blocker-not-an-occupancy-question\n`dumpsys power | grep mWakefulness` reports `Dozing` or `Asleep` when the phone's own screen timeout has\nlocked it, distinct from the founder actively using it. `KEYCODE_WAKEUP` lights the screen but does not\nbypass a secure lock; `dumpsys deviceidle | grep mScreenLocked` confirms whether it is still locked.\nMeasured 2026-08-31: a UAT session's `am start` and tap landed silently on the lock screen mid-run.\n\nThis is not the \"never wait for Saurabh\" case in `../rules/tools-and-apps.md`. That rule is about not\npausing for his own use of an unlocked phone; a secure lock needs his PIN, which the harness does not have\nand must never try to guess. Check wakefulness before trusting a tap or screenshot, and if locked, report\n`NEED YOU` and stop rather than sending input into a black screen.\n\n## RULE: the-emulator-cannot-answer-the-questions-that-matter\n`scripts/enviouswispr-emulator.sh` boots an AVD and installs the debug APK. Use it for Compose layout,\nnavigation and permission flows; it cannot answer anything about the vendor runtime, the Samsung side\nbutton, Samsung window layering, battery, or thermals, and a latency claim measured there is not evidence.\n**Emulator FIRST for screen-only work** (founder 2026-09-01: \"stop using my phone for testing\"): a\nchange that touches no capture, ASR, polish engine, insertion or model-loading code validates on the\nemulator and takes the phone only for a question the emulator cannot answer; a plan's hardware UAT section\nfor a screen-only change names the emulator.\n\n**It CAN hear speech and HAS real editors** (Chrome, Messages, Gmail, Gboard on `EnviousWispr_Android_16`;\nSamsung-specific behaviour is not testable). Two switches gate the microphone: `-allow-host-audio` on the\nlaunch line PERMITS it, and `adb -s emulator-5554 emu avd hostmicon` turns it ON (not persisted; without\nit every take records silence and `AsrService` logs `textChars=0` while the pipeline reports success).\n`scripts/enviouswispr-emulator.sh` runs `hostmicon` on every launch. The canonical audio feed is RULE:\nfeed-emulator-audio-over-grpc-injectaudio-not-blackhole; the cable path (`say_into_emulator()`,\n`SwitchAudioSource -t input -s \"BlackHole 2ch\"`, `say -a \"BlackHole 2ch\"`, needs `brew install\nblackhole-2ch switchaudio-osx`) is the fallback, and the speaker path is retired (founder 2026-09-13).\nTwo traps: `adb emu kill` takes up to 20 s to release the microphone, and an emulator launched inside that\nwindow logs `coreaudio: Could not initialize record` and hears nothing until relaunched; the launch script\nbackgrounds the emulator, so run it with `run_in_background`. Parakeet is placed by PROCEDURE:\nplace-a-model-by-hand (`model-delivery.md`).\n\n## FACT: the-lips-bubble-uat\nThe floating lips button (#135, PR #137) was exercised on the emulator with these probes on 2026-09-12:\n`emulator-5556` (AVD `EnviousWispr_Bubble`, Android 16, Gboard, Chrome, `-allow-host-audio`), debug build\nof `feat/135-lips-bubble-on-brand` at `25a9ac6` (the same three commits, copied off the onboarding branch onto #119). The overlay window is found by its title,\n`EnviousWispr recording controls`, in `dumpsys window windows`; on this emulator it is also visible in\n`screencap`, unlike the S26.
