The matrix, driven by the\n   377\tside button with Gboard the default keyboard: a plain field (Messages); a rich editor (Gmail, Google\n   378\tDocs); a browser field (Chrome address bar, a web form); a terminal or code editor; a chat app; a password\n   379\tfield, treated as ordinary by decision (`../rules/architecture-rules.md` FACT:\n   380\tthere-is-no-sensitive-field-guard-and-that-is-decided; until #11 lands it still diverts to copy-only, so\n   381\tthat row proves the OLD behaviour); a stale or unsupported target, which must keep the transcript on the\n   382\tclipboard and say so; and **back-to-back** (dictate, insert, immediately dictate again, asserting the\n   383\tsecond transcript reaches the editor), where the P1 lives (#132).\n   384\t\n   385\t## FACT: what-gmail-actually-does-to-insertion-2026-08-30\n   386\tMeasured on the S26 from the founder's own dictations. Four symptoms, one cause.\n   387\t\n   388\t- **The insertion succeeds and is reported as unverified.** All 21 attempts logged `action=SET_TEXT\n   389\t  textMatched=true ... caret=0/0 expectedCaret=34`; the only failing clause in\n   390\t  `AccessibilityInsertionRules.isVerified` is the caret, because Gmail's compose reports `0/0` wherever\n   391\t  the insertion went. **The caret is NOT cosmetic, so do not drop it from the check**: it decides WHERE the\n   392\t  words go, and a `0/0` read puts them at the start of the field (\"it also sucks other text to it\").\n   393\t- **It destroys the user's whitespace.** `SET_TEXT` replaces the WHOLE field with a string composed from a\n   394\t  lossy read-back (`AccessibilityNodeInfo.text` normalises whitespace), so lines merge. Do NOT relax\n   395\t  `isVerified`; a check that accepted this ships silent data loss in real drafts.\n   396\t- **Why the destructive path was taken:** `normalizedSelection` returns `null` for `-1/-1` and the code\n   397\t  fell back to paste on that null, but Gmail reports `0/0`, a PLAUSIBLE value, not a sentinel\n   398\t  (`../rules/validation-discipline.md` FACT: silent-empty-traps). The log corroborates: `ACTION_SET_SELECTION`\n   399\t  to 34 followed by a read of `0/0`, so this editor reports no caret at all.\n   400\t- Closing and reopening Gmail fixes it, so the app works from a stale view of that editor.\n   401\t\n   402\tResolved by #141's one-route-one-write rule (commit route, then paste, no `ACTION_SET_TEXT`); the macOS\n   403\tcascade for comparison is `Sources/EnviousWisprPipeline/PasteCascadeExecutor.swift`, and the two shipping\n   404\tcompetitors neither check the caret nor rewrite a non-empty compose\n   405\t(`docs/internal/competitor-insertion-study.md`). **Reproducing it needs the founder's own hand:** every\n   406\tGmail compose opened over ADB reported `NO_PINNED_TARGET`, so two runs are comparable only when the\n   407\teditor was opened the same way.\n   408\t\n   409\t## FACT: the-141-one-write-emulator-uat\n   410\tRun 2026-09-13 on `emulator-5554` (`EnviousWispr_Android_16`, Gboard, Chrome, host mic on). Editor: a\n   411\tlocal page from the Mac (`http://10.0.2.2:8765`) with a `<textarea>` holding two paragraphs and a blank\n   412\tline, and a mirror `<pre>` showing `JSON.stringify(value)`. Oracle: the mirror, never the clipboard or log.\n   413\t\n   414\tChunk 1 (debug build of `feat/141-insertion-cascade` at `52ef940`, paste only): two takes, both `route=PASTE ...\n   415\toutcome=VERIFIED` (attempts 2 then 14, the second because Chrome's node lagged the paste), blank line\n   416\tintact, each sentence once at the caret with the seam space. Capitals and the trailing period come from\n   417\tthe cleanup limb. `Clipboard changed during insertion; preserving the newer clipboard` after a success is\n   418\t`ClipboardService: Denying clipboard access ... not in focus` (the Android 10+ background read limit), so\n   419\tthe user's previous clip is not restored.\n   420\t\n   421\tChunk 2 (`feat/141-commit-route` at `2fe39dc`, voice through the cable): four dictations, every line\n   422\t`route=COMMIT written=true returned=VOID outcome=VERIFIED` (caret after \"Hi team,\", end of draft,\n   423\tmid-draft right after an `adb install -r`, and a short mid-draft take with `evidence=SURROUNDING`), no\n   424\tclipboard write, seam and capital right. Log shapes: `Input started on the pipe: package=... restarting=true`\n   425\tat every focus change; `Commit route not eligible: <reason>` (`no input method`, `input not started`,\n   426\t`session package differs`, `focused window differs`, `pinned editor not focused`) when paste is taken;\n   427\t`The pipe read surrounding text: before=<n> after=<n> offset=<n>`. Chrome answers `offset=-1` (unknown), so\n   428\ta window shorter than the compare length hands over to the node judge (`evidence=NODE`), while a payload\n   429\tshort enough for the window verifies by the windows (`evidence=SURROUNDING`). The service's own `withPinnedNode` proof is the\n   430\teligibility test, not a FOCUS_INPUT search from the window root. NOT RUN: Gmail on this AVD, Messages, the S26.\n   431\t\n   432\t## FACT: the-play-store-emulator-for-gmail-and-chatgpt\n   433\tA second AVD `EnviousWispr_Android_16_Play` (2026-09-13): `pixel_9_pro_xl` on\n   434\t`system-images;android-36;google_apis_playstore;arm64-v8a`, `PlayStore.enabled=yes`, `hw.ramSize=4096`,\n   435\t`hw.keyboard=yes`. Launch: `EW_AVD_NAME=EnviousWispr_Android_16_Play bash scripts/enviouswispr-emulator.sh`;\n   436\tboth AVDs use `emulator-5554`, so run ONE at a time. Signed in as `hello@enviouslabs.co` (screen lock PIN\n   437\t`1234`), Gmail synced, ChatGPT installed, Parakeet placed by hand, S1-mini pulled by onboarding.\n   438\t\n   439\t- **Open Gmail compose with the app's own Compose button** (`ComposeActivityGmail`); a `mailto:` intent\n   440\t  opens `ComposeActivityGmailExternal`, whose body discovery does NOT see (`Bubble discovery found=false`),\n   441\t  which an earlier session misread as \"the emulator cannot test Gmail\".\n   442\t- **Compose survives a settings round trip only through BACK:** `am start -n\n   443\t  com.envi.wispr/.ui.SettingsActivity` on top of Gmail, tap, then `KEYCODE_BACK` twice; any intent aimed\n   444\t  at Gmail pops the compose to the conversation (draft saved; reopen with the pencil).\n   445\t- **Under a host load average above 50 the first `injectAudio` take can decode as silence** (`textChars=0`,\n   446\t  recogniser init 83 s); check `uptime` before blaming the mic or the build.\n   447\t- Gmail UAT 2026-09-13 (`feat/141-commit-route` at `1277d9f`): one commit at the caret, `route=COMMIT ...\n   448\t  outcome=VERIFIED attempts=1 ms=66 target=com.google.android.gm`, no clipboard write; Gmail answers\n   449\t  `getSurroundingText` with `offset=-1`, so `evidence=NODE`. The Mac `say` voice mis-hears words; the\n   450\t  oracle is placement, seam and capital.\n   451\t\n   452\t## RULE: feed-emulator-audio-over-grpc-injectaudio-not-blackhole\n   453\t**Canonical way to feed spoken audio to the emulator, reliable back-to-back (proven 2026-09-13, #141):**\n   454\tstream PCM into the virtual mic over the emulator gRPC `injectAudio` RPC, bypassing coreaudio and\n   455\tBlackHole. Since #177 (2026-09-20) the harness owns every step: `launch_emulator()` (boots with `-grpc\n   456\t8554`), `set_host_mic(False)` (over gRPC, journaled), `inject_audio(pcm)` inside `open_recorder()`,\n   457\t`dictate_emulator(sentence)` for one take judged by the editor's text; the loose scripts are gone. On top\n   458\tof it, `scripts/uat/rail_signals.py` (#151, 2026-09-15): known sounds (silence, three tones, a sweep, hiss, 4 Hz\n   459\tbursts) injected during a take, the pill screen-recorded, every bar measured per frame from its pixels\n   460\tand judged against what the rail must draw. It found the tap pill's mapping skipping five of eleven bands\n   461\twhile the published picture was right, which no spoken take could have shown. Two traps it met: with the\n   462\thost microphone off the emulator's own source ramps up for about a second after the microphone opens\n   463\t(it lit every bar on a rate-limited noise floor, so the floor became a windowed minimum), and a hold is\n   464\tdriven with `input swipe x y x y <ms>` on the bubble while the packets stream.\n   465\t\n   466\t- **Emulator 37.2.8+ (canary, `sdkmanager --channel=3 emulator`).** 37.1.11 crashes on the SECOND\n   467\t  recording of a session (`coreaudio: Could not initialize record`) on both paths. **After upgrading the\n   468\t  binary you MUST `-wipe-data` on next boot** (old userdata makes every activity unresolvable); that\n   469\t  erases the AVD, so budget the re-setup.\n   470\t- **Launch with `-grpc 8554`** (console port + 3000; unauthenticated on localhost). Client: `grpcurl`\n   471\t  (brew); proto at `~/Android/sdk/emulator/lib/emulator_controller.proto`, service\n   472\t  `android.emulation.control.EmulatorController`.\n   473\t- **Host mic OFF is the emulator's RESTING state, and nothing switches it inside a take.** A capture\n   474\t  opened right after a host-mic switch dropped the injected audio 4 times in 25 (`Transcription result\n   475\t  received (chars=0)`, `NO_SPEECH`); 0 in 10 with no switch inside the take (2026-09-20, #181). The\n   476\t  mechanism is the emulator's. `launch_emulator()`, `dictate_emulator()` and the BlackHole take's cleanup\n   477\t  all call `_rest_host_mic_off()`; gRPC `setMicrophoneState` flips the same switch the old console\n   478\t  command did and `getMicrophoneState` READS it, so the console is not used.\n   479\t- **Per take, in order** (what `dictate_emulator()` does): rest the mic off (usually already off);\n   480\t  `open_recorder()` (the mic must be open or injectAudio resets); wait ~3 s; `inject_audio(pcm)`; stop.\n   481\t  Half a second of silence is appended to the PCM, or the last word is cut (\"to Ma.\" for \"tomorrow\",\n   482\t  first live take 2026-09-20).\n   483\t- **PCM + packets:** s16le mono 48000 Hz raw; `inject_audio` is the ONLY packet builder: newline-delimited\n   484\t  JSON AudioPackets of ~100 ms (9600 bytes), each with a `format` block AND a `timestamp` (epoch us;\n   485\t  empty crashed the emulator); `MODE_UNSPECIFIED`.\n   486\t\n   487\t**BlackHole is the fallback only:** one take per boot; never switch the Mac's default input while the\n   488\temulator runs; `hostmicon` once at boot, never per take; never run another recorder on BlackHole.\n   489\t\n   490\t## FACT: silent-physical-phone-audio-injection-for-night-uat\n   491\tThe physical-phone counterpart to the emulator gRPC path, and the DEFAULT way to run a real take on the\n   492\tS26 without speaker sound (founder wants night UAT while the household sleeps). Owner:\n   493\t`scripts/uat/silent-audio/` (`README.md` is the contract, `run.py` the one call, `SilentAudio.java` the\n   494\t`app_process` injector). It feeds the test PCM through an `AudioPolicy` `REMOTE_SUBMIX` injection mix\n   495\tscoped to `com.envi.wispr`'s UID; the authorized ADB shell already holds the routing permission, so there\n   496\tis no APK change, no root, no volume change, and no audio leaves the phone. Media volume is asserted\n   497\tunchanged; it never touches a speaker track.\n   498\t\n   499\tOne call, into an already focused empty editor on the unlocked phone:\n   500\t```bash\n   501\tpython3 scripts/uat/silent-audio/run.py --serial 100.94.206.47:5555 \\\n   502\t  --pcm /data/local/tmp/<fixture>.pcm --expect '<exact editor text>' --receipt /tmp/<dir>\n   503\t```\n   504\tFixture is raw 16 kHz mono s16le PCM already ON THE PHONE, rendered SILENTLY (Azure TTS to PCM, or\n   505\t`say`+`ffmpeg` per `README.md`), never recorded from the phone.\n   506\t\n   507\t- **Gotcha: do NOT `adb logcat -c` right before the run.** `run.py`'s precondition reads the log for a\n   508\t  prior recording start/stop; an empty log blocks it (`the log holds neither the start nor the end of a\n   509\t  take`). Seed one benign start/stop first (toggle the recorder on the home screen with no field focused:\n   510\t  `am start -n com.envi.wispr/.ui.VoiceInputActivity --ez toggle true` then `--ez stop true`).\n   511\t- **One phone, exclusive** while it runs; it drives the real exported recorder.\n   512\t- **After a Play update or a force-stop on Android 16 the enabled service stays UNBOUND until the app is\n   513\t  launched once** (`dumpsys accessibility`: named under `Enabled services`, absent from `Bound services`,\n   514\t  nothing under `Crashed services`); the write-empty-then-set dance alone did not bind it, `open_app` did\n   515\t  (measured 2026-09-21 on build 154). Launch the app, then check `bound()`.\n   516\t- **`restore()` with a journaled switch needs the app's own tab row on screen**: it re-reads the switch's\n   517\t  page, so from Gmail or Chrome it raises `the four tabs are not all on screen`. Open the app first\n   518\t  (`open_app('com.envi.wispr')`), then `restore()`; the emulator take helpers do this in their `finally`.\n   519\t- Verified 2026-09-16 on internal build 134 into a Chrome web input: 4/4 `route=COMMIT outcome=VERIFIED`,\n   520\t  ~130 ms, `attempts=2` (the pipe's re-read recovers on the second attempt), the editor's own text\n   521\t  matched, media volume 7 to 7. Fail-closed: cancels the take and unregisters the mix on any error, with\n   522\t  an on-phone 60 s deadline as a backstop.\n   523\t\n   524\t## RULE: keep-the-emulator-host-mic-stable-during-synthetic-uat\n   525\tThe emulator hears through QEMU's coreaudio RECORD device, and on macOS + BlackHole that capture is\n   526\tfragile once the emulator is running (measured 2026-09-13, #141). Two things silently kill it, after\n   527\twhich every take records silence (`AsrService ... textChars=0`, guest log `failed to create alsa source\n   528\t... creating a tone source instead`, host `/tmp/<AVD>.log` `coreaudio: Could not initialize record ...\n   529\tkAudioHardwareIllegalOperationError`), and ONLY an emulator restart recovers it:\n   530\t1. **Switching the Mac's default INPUT device while the emulator runs.** So set the input to the cable\n   531\t   ONCE before launch (`SwitchAudioSource -t input -s \"BlackHole 2ch\"`) and never change it during the\n   532\t   session; `say_into_emulator`'s per-take switch is wrong on this rig.\n   533\t2. **Calling `adb emu avd hostmicon` per take.** It re-inits coreaudio record, which intermittently\n   534\t   fails and drops to the tone source. Call hostmicon ONCE at boot (enviouswispr-emulator.sh does), then\n   535\t   never again for the session.\n   536\tAlso never run `ffmpeg`/`rec`/another recorder on `BlackHole 2ch` while the emulator runs; grabbing the\n   537\tdevice breaks QEMU's capture the same way. A take with `textChars=0` plus a tone-source line means the\n   538\tmic is dead: restart the emulator, do not retry the take.\n   539\t\n   540\t## RULE: record-the-screen-through-a-uat-take\n   541\tFounder 2026-09-13: record the screen through every UAT take, because a screenshot catches one instant\n   542\tand misses the pill state, a vanished bubble, or a toast. Start `adb -s <serial> shell screenrecord\n   543\t--time-limit <n> /sdcard/uat.mp4` in the background BEFORE the take, run the whole take inside it, `adb\n   544\tpull` it and watch it; it is for the tester, not the founder unless he asks. And prove a pathway by hand,\n   545\tone observed step at a time, BEFORE wrapping it in a script (founder: \"scripts only after you proven the\n   546\tcorrect pathways\").\n   547\t\n   548\t## FACT: the-auto-paste-liveness-uat\n   549\tThe named evidence for any change to the auto-paste readiness signal. **The oracle is the `Bound services`\n   550\tline**; a recipe that greps `Enabled services` confirms the bug as a PASS. Executed 2026-08-29 on the\n   551\tAndroid 16 emulator for steps 1 to 5 and 7 (passed: the row went Ready → `Turned on but not connected` →\n   552\tReady with the app untouched); steps 6 and 8 and the two silences are NOT RUN (they need a real dictation\n   553\tinto a third-party editor).\n   554\t\n   555\tLevers: `settings put secure accessibility_enabled 0` does NOT unbind; `settings put` with an empty string\n   556\tfails with `Bad arguments`; `settings delete secure enabled_accessibility_services` unbinds (and revokes,\n   557\tso it stages the UI transition, not the setting divergence, which only a real crash produces: FACT:\n   558\tthe-issue-16-state-cannot-be-staged-by-settings). `am crash` kills the screen the assertion is read from,\n   559\tbecause the service and `SettingsActivity` share the default process.\n   560\t\n   561\t```bash\n   562\tADB=~/Android/sdk/platform-tools/adb\n   563\t$ADB shell dumpsys accessibility | grep -E 'Bound services|Enabled services|Crashed services'\n   564\t$ADB shell settings get secure enabled_accessibility_services   # RECORD THIS, step 7 restores it\n   565\t```\n   566\t\n   567\t1. Record that baseline: `Bound services` names us, `Crashed services` empty.\n   568\t2. Open the app on Settings: Auto-paste access says `Ready for right-button dictation`, Insert chip green.\n   569\t3. `$ADB shell settings delete secure enabled_accessibility_services`.\n   570\t4. **Without touching the phone**, the Permissions page's auto-paste row reads `Turned on but not\n   571\t   connected` and the Insert chip is red (the acceptance criterion; reachable only because the signal is\n   572\t   pushed).\n   573\t5. Re-run dumpsys: `Bound services` no longer names us.\n   574\t6. With the service unbound, dictate into a third-party editor: ONE toast `Copied. Press and hold, then\n   575\t   tap Paste.`; paste and confirm the words. No buzz, nothing in the shade (pull it down), no red line on\n   576\t   the History row.\n   577\t7. Restore the recorded value verbatim (`settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services <recorded>`);\n   578\t   without touching the app the row returns to Ready; re-read the setting to prove the restore landed.\n   579\t8. History shows the transcript and NO status line.\n   580\t\n   581\t**Unclean-stop marker, a separate run:** `$ADB shell am crash com.envi.wispr`, relaunch, `$ADB logcat -d |\n   582\tgrep 'Reconnected after an unclean stop'`; repeat after an off-and-on cycle in Accessibility settings, where\n   583\tits absence is the `MIN-1` regression.\n   584\t\n   585\t**Two silences are part of the acceptance:** a user who never granted the permission (disable, dictate,\n   586\twords land on the clipboard, nothing else); and a dictation with no field (service bound, dictate from the\n   587\ttile: `$ADB logcat -d | grep 'handoff='` reads `NO_PINNED_TARGET`, shade empty).\n   588\t\n   589\t## FACT: the-issue-16-state-cannot-be-staged-by-settings\n   590\t**Measured on the S26, 2026-08-30, running the `fix/16-auto-paste-readiness` build.**\n   591\t\n   592\tThe state issue #16 describes is `Enabled services` naming us while the service is DEAD: permission TRUE,\n   593\tbinding FALSE. **No settings lever reaches it on Android 16.**\n   594\t\n   595\t- `settings put secure accessibility_enabled 0` does not unbind at all.\n   596\t- `settings delete secure enabled_accessibility_services` unbinds, but it also revokes the permission, so\n   597\t  the app correctly classifies the result as NOT_PERMITTED — a user who never granted it — and stays\n   598\t  silent by design.\n   599\t- Turning the service off in Accessibility settings does the same thing by hand.\n   600\t\n   601\t**Only a genuine service crash produces permission-true-and-unbound**, which is what the founder saw and\n   602\twhat `Crashed services` reported. So a UAT that deletes the setting proves the clipboard fallback and the\n   603\tNOT_PERMITTED silence, and CANNOT prove the message a permitted-but-dead user gets.\n   604\t\n   605\t**What this means for anyone testing #16:** the readiness half is provable, the announcement half is not,\n   606\tuntil the service can be crashed on demand. The unclean-stop marker is the nearest instrument.\n   607\t\n   608\t## FACT: what-the-2026-08-30-run-actually-proved\n   609\tEnd to end on the phone, with the `fix/16-auto-paste-readiness` build installed:\n   610\t\n   611\t- **Auto-paste alive:** dictation reached the Messages compose field. `Insertion completed via SET_TEXT\n   612\t  after 1 attempt(s)`, `handoff=SCHEDULED`, and the polished sentence was visible in the field with cleanup\n   613\t  punctuation applied.\n   614\t- **Auto-paste unbound:** `handoff=SERVICE_NOT_RUNNING`, the transcript reached the clipboard, and pasting\n   615\t  it into a fresh field returned the text. The clipboard fallback works.\n   616\t- **The app stayed silent**, correctly, because the same lever that unbinds also revokes, so the state it\n   617\t  saw was NOT_PERMITTED. That is the class-A suppression working, not a missing announcement.\n   618\t\n   619\t**Caveat on the audio, stated rather than hidden:** the transcript did not match the sentence queued for\n   620\t`SpeakerPlaybackActivity`; the microphone captured ambient speech instead. The pipeline ran end to end and\n   621\tthe insertion and fallback paths are evidenced, but this run is NOT evidence that the TTS fixture played.\n   622\tCheck media volume before relying on the helper for content-specific assertions.\n   623\t\n   624\t## FACT: which-microphone-actually-captured\n   625\t\"Words appeared\" does not say which microphone produced them, and that distinction is the whole of\n   626\t[issue #26](https://github.com/Envious-Labs-LLC/EnviousWispr-Android/issues/26). Read the bound input\n   627\tdevice WHILE recording:\n   628\t\n   629\t```bash\n   630\tadb shell dumpsys media.audio_flinger | sed -n '/^Input thread/,/^Output thread/p' | grep -iE \"Input device:|AUDIO_DEVICE_IN\"\n   631\t```\n   632\t\n   633\tWith no headset it must print `AUDIO_DEVICE_IN_BUILTIN_MIC` — run that control first, because an empty\n   634\tresult reads exactly like a Bluetooth capture. The `CFG_EVENT_CREATE_AUDIO_PATCH` line in the same block\n   635\trecords each route change with a timestamp, so it also answers what happened mid-take.\n   636\t\n   637\t## FACT: what-the-2026-09-03-silence-run-proved-and-what-it-did-not\n   638\tThe #5 auto-stop run on the S26, debug build, phone SECURE-LOCKED (everything below needs no screen).\n   639\t\n   640\t- `getMinBufferSize` returns **1280** bytes for 16 kHz mono PCM16, so the 32,000-byte floor binds\n   641\t  (`Buffer sizes: minimum=1280 coerced=32000 read=8192`); the one-second read granularity the change\n   642\t  removed was real.\n   643\t- The detector runs in `com.envi.wispr:vad` by PID and exits when the last client unbinds.\n   644\t- **Killing the detector mid-recording does not disturb the recording**: `run-as com.envi.wispr kill -9\n   645\t  <vad-pid>`, then `:audio` logged `Auto-stop abandoned for this take` and the take ran to 12.0 s.\n   646\t  `run-as com.envi.wispr.test` CANNOT kill a `com.envi.wispr` process (different UID, `kill` returns 1,\n   647\t  the test still passes); re-read the pid after any kill.\n   648\t- **A quiet room never ends a take** (12.0 s, `TERMINAL_REASON_MANUAL`): the control that matters most.\n   649\t- Also proven over the real binder: real speech scores CONTINUE and the silence after it ends the take,\n   650\t  not on the first silent block; a start from an older take is refused outright and its blocks with it;\n   651\t  a wrongly sized block is refused; the switch off means no\n   652\t  detector; an out-of-range pause refuses auto-stop while recording continues.\n   653\t- **Same evening, unlocked, founder's hand:** a silence-ended take inserted into Gmail (6.4 s, 43\n   654\t  characters, `handoff=SCHEDULED`) and WhatsApp; the switch and slider survive a restart and an install.\n   655\t  Receipt: `.validation/runs/20260904T004512Z-53755bb`.\n   656\t\n   657\t**The stop line names the ending** (`endTakeLocked` writes `Stopped by <ending>.`; the time limit and a\n   658\tcapture failure write their own lines from `captureLoop`). Never read the ORDER of log lines:\n   659\t`claimEnding` clears `isRecording` before `recording_stop`, so a silence stop and a button press log in the\n   660\tsame order. `a stop request` is NOT proof the user pressed stop (`onDestroy` ends a take by the same\n   661\troute); telling them apart needs a new AIDL reason (#114).\n   662\t\n   663\t**A Gmail window opened over ADB does not pin** (`NO_PINNED_TARGET` on the branch AND on `main`), the same\n   664\tartifact as FACT: what-gmail-actually-does-to-insertion-2026-08-30; two runs are comparable only when the\n   665\teditor was opened the same way.\n   666\t\n   667\t## FACT: the-polish-policy-propagation-uat\n   668\tThe recipe for #69, and for any change to how the engine learns the polish mode. Switch to This phone on the screen. Dictate into Samsung Notes. `logcat -s PolishService` must show\n   674\t   `S1-mini loaded` on the SAME pid, and the History card must read \"Polished by S1-mini by Superwhisper\".\n   675\t3. Switch to a cloud provider with a saved key; dictate; the History card names the provider.\n   676\t4. Switch back to Off; dictate; the History card reads \"AI Polish was off\".\n   677\tNo app kill between steps. Restore the mode the phone had before the run.\n   678\t\n   679\t## FACT: the-residency-campaign\n   680\t`scripts/uat/residency-campaign.sh <runs> <short.pcm> <long.pcm>` is the #72 measurement: real dictations\n   681\tthrough the speaker in four warm-up shapes × rested and loaded memory, with an on-device sampler\n   682\t(`scripts/uat/device-sampler.sh`) and `scripts/uat/residency-report.py` for the table. It refuses a phone it\n   683\tcannot measure honestly and restores the override file and the screen timeout from a trap. Traps it was\n   684\tbuilt around, each measured 2026-09-01:\n   685\t\n   686\t- **A Bluetooth headset steals the speaker**, so the fixture plays into the founder's ears and the phone\n   687\t  hears nothing: the transcript comes back empty and the run looks like an ASR failure.\n   688\t- **`grep -q` under `pipefail` refuses on a MATCH** (`../rules/validation-discipline.md` FACT:\n   689\t  silent-empty-traps): the preflight refused an awake phone until every probe captured its output first.\n   690\t- **The screen timeout ends the campaign silently.** A dimmed phone is woken with `KEYCODE_WAKEUP`; a\n   691\t  locked one is refused (FACT above). The script raises the timeout to thirty minutes and restores it.\n   692\t- **The stratum is derived, never labelled.** `am kill` before a cold run must leave no `:polish` pid, and\n   693\t  the report classifies cold versus cached from the pid recorded before the run.\n   694\t- **The spoken fixture comes from Azure Speech** (`phone-audio-playback.md`); the eleven-second one yields\n   695\t  about 175 characters, so a transcript outside 120 to 260 characters marks the run failed rather than\n   696\t  averaged.\n   697\t\n   698\t## FACT: the-staged-polish-timeout\n   699\tLocal polish has an engine deadline and the session a watchdog (#75). Neither can be staged with a real\n   700\twedge, so a debug build reads two per-request files under `files/debug/` (integers in milliseconds,\n   701\tdebuggable builds only, out-of-range values ignored): `polish-deadline-ms` replaces the cooperative\n   702\tdeadline (hard = value + 2 s), and `polish-stall-ms` holds the worker BEFORE generation, outside the\n   703\tcooperative timeout, which is what a wedge looks like. Recipe, This phone selected, fixture in place\n   704\t(`phone-audio-playback.md`), `scripts/uat/dictate-once.sh` for each dictation:\n   705\t\n   706\t1. Cooperative path: `run-as com.envi.wispr sh -c 'mkdir -p files/debug && printf 1 > files/debug/polish-deadline-ms'`.\n   707\t   Expect `reason=LOCAL_TIMEOUT`, `engine process will end`, the deterministic text handed off, `Ending the\n   708\t   polish engine process` within a second, `pidof com.envi.wispr:polish` empty. Remove the file and dictate\n   709\t   again: `Ready on GPU` on a NEW pid and `reason=POLISHED`. Measured 2026-09-01: expiry to exit 81 ms.\n   710\t2. Hard path: `printf 30000 > files/debug/polish-stall-ms` with no deadline file. Expect the shipped hard\n   711\t   timer at 12 s: `Local polish deadline expired` while the worker is still asleep, then the exit; the\n   712\t   session receives `LOCAL_TIMEOUT` before its own 15 s watchdog. Measured 2026-09-01: expiry at\n   713\t   12.0 s from the stall, `latencyMs=12011`, exit 100 ms later.\n   714\t3. Watchdog: `printf 20000 > files/debug/polish-deadline-ms` (hard 22 s, above the watchdog) with the\n   715\t   30 s stall still in place. Expect `Polish watchdog fired` at about 15 s, the engine cancel logged, and\n   716\t   the fallback published with `WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT`; the engine ends itself as soon as the session\n   717\t   unbinds (`destroyed with 1 local request(s) in flight`), before its own 22 s timer. Remove both\n   718\t   files. Measured 2026-09-01: watchdog at 15.0 s from the stall, exit 180 ms later.\n   719\t4. Cancel: start a dictation with the 40 s fixture, stop it, tap Cancel on the \"Preparing your words\"\n   720\t   notification within the transcription window (about 3 s): expect `Cancelled while processing`, no\n   721\t   text, no History row, and either the engine's cancel or the transcript dropped by the state check.\n   722\t   Driving it: our notification's body and actions are NOT in the `uiautomator dump` (only its timestamp\n   723\t   is), so read positions off `screencap`. With ours newest at the top of the shade (1080x2340): chevron\n   724\t   at (972,950); expanded, Stop at (302,1097) and Cancel at (778,1097); the processing notification's\n   725\t   single Cancel is centred at (540,1145), and (540,1097) hits it. Tapping the body fires the content\n   726\t   intent, which STOPS the recording. A longer recording widens the window (84 s of audio gave 2 s of\n   727\t   transcription plus polish). Measured 2026-09-01: Stop to Cancel 2.1 s, ASR unbound 140 ms later.\n   728\tRestore: both files removed, the mode the phone had before, engine process ended.\n   729\t\n   730\t## FACT: the-polish-outcome-uat\n   731\tThe recipe for #77 and for any change to what the user is told about a failed polish. Stage a real\n   732\tprovider rejection without spending: on the AI Polish screen choose Cloud, Gemini, type any non-blank key\n   733\t(the screen's Check is a format check), tap Check, tap a model; the key is saved in the Keystore.\n   734\tDictate the 11 s fixture from the launcher: expect\n   735\t`reason=HTTP_KEY_REJECTED status=400` (the real Gemini 400 body carries `API_KEY_INVALID`),\n   736\t`Polish notice shown: KEY_REJECTED`, the toast \"Polish failed. Using raw text.\", a silent notification\n   737\t\"AI polish failed\" with the full sentence, and the History card's polish line \"AI polish failed: Gemini\n   738\trejected your API key. Check or replace it in Settings.\" over \"Cleaned up on this phone\". Measured\n   739\t2026-09-01. Two traps found the same day: the app had never declared the Internet permission, so every\n   740\tcloud request failed in 34 ms as `NETWORK` (fixed in #77); and a toast shows two lines and truncates the\n   741\trest, which is why the reason lives in a notification. Restore: \"Remove saved provider and key\" on the\n   742\tscreen, mode back to Off.\n   743\t\n   744\t## RULE: report-a-skipped-device-test-as-not-run\n   745\tInstrumented tests use `assumeTrue` for preconditions such as the PCM fixture, so a missing precondition\n   746\treports SKIPPED. A skipped receipt is not a passed receipt. Say \"not run\", never \"passed\".\n   747\t\n   748\t## FACT: shizuku-is-not-ours\n   749\tShizuku grants shell-level permissions to on-device tooling. EnviousWispr does not depend on it; it matters\n   750\tonly for the phone's own Claude Code autonomy. Owner: [phone-bridge.md](phone-bridge.md).\n     1\t# Phone Audio Playback\n     2\t\n     3\tThis page owns the repeatable way to play spoken test audio through the physical phone. The audio is\n     4\tgenerated or decoded on the phone itself. It is not streamed from the MacBook and does not use the\n     5\tMacBook speakers.\n     6\t\n     7\t## FACT: the-test-helper-lives-only-in-the-test-apk\n     8\t\n     9\t`SpeakerPlaybackActivity` is declared only by the Android test APK. Installing or launching only the\n    10\tnormal application cannot expose it. The helper uses Android's offline US text-to-speech voice, speaks at\n    11\t0.85 speed and full per-utterance volume, then closes itself.\n    12\t\n    13\tThe helper reads its custom sentence from the test package's private\n    14\t`files/speaker-utterance.txt`. It does not read an intent extra. The file is deleted after it is read. If\n    15\tthe file is missing, empty, or larger than 500 bytes, the helper says:\n    16\t\n    17\t> This is a physical phone insertion test.\n    18\t\n    19\t## PROCEDURE: play-a-custom-sentence-through-the-phone\n    20\t\n    21\tFrom the repository root:\n    22\t\n    23\t```bash\n    24\tSERIAL=100.94.206.47:5555\n    25\tPROJECT=/Users/m4pro_sv/Developer/EnviousLabs/EnviousWispr-Android\n    26\t\n    27\tcd \"$PROJECT\"\n    28\t./gradlew :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest --no-daemon --console=plain\n    29\t\n    30\tadb -s \"$SERIAL\" install -r \"$PROJECT/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk\"\n    31\tadb -s \"$SERIAL\" install -r -t \"$PROJECT/app/build/outputs/apk/androidTest/debug/app-debug-androidTest.apk\"\n    32\t\n    33\tadb -s \"$SERIAL\" shell run-as com.envi.wispr.test mkdir -p files\n    34\tprintf '%s' 'This sentence is playing through my phone speaker.' \\\n    35\t  | adb -s \"$SERIAL\" shell \\\n    36\t      'run-as com.envi.wispr.test sh -c \"cat > files/speaker-utterance.txt\"'\n    37\t\n    38\tadb -s \"$SERIAL\" shell am start \\\n    39\t  -n com.envi.wispr.test/com.envi.wispr.SpeakerPlaybackActivity\n    40\t```\n    41\t\n    42\tUse `-t` when installing the Android test APK because Android marks it as test-only. A missing fixture makes\n    66\tthe instrumented test skip; report that as not run, never passed.\n    67\t\n    68\t## RULE: diagnose-the-right-audio-path\n    69\t\n    70\t- If no sound plays, first confirm that both APKs are installed and that phone media volume is audible.\n    71\t- Do not pass the sentence as an activity intent extra; the helper ignores it.\n    72\t- Do not use MacBook audio as evidence when the phone and laptop are in different locations.\n    73\t- Do not confuse offline text-to-speech playback with the PCM fixture used by the full pipeline test.\n    74\t- **`termux-tts-speak` and `termux-media-player` BLOCK FOREVER** when Termux:API is not answering, and a\n    75\t  blocked SSH call reads as a slow one. Design\\n    69\\t\\n    70\\t### Part H, the harness (`scripts/uat/wispr_eyes.py`)\\n    71\\tH1. **The take's evidence is parsed, not eyeballed.** `_insertion_line(text)` (proposed) parses one `insertion api=` line into `{api, route, written, returned, evidence, outcome, attempts, ms, overrun, target}`; `last_take()` returns it as `insertion` (the stale `Insertion completed via` key goes) and counts `insertion api=` lines in its window (`insertions` (proposed)). `dictate_emulator` and `debug_insert` require `insertions == 1`, `outcome == \\\"VERIFIED\\\"`, `written == \\\"true\\\"`, `target == target_package`, else `ISSUE: …` naming the field; the route is its own line `VERIFIED: route=COMMIT` (or `PASTE`, still a pass; `route` is reported, never assumed). `dictate_emulator(..., route=None)` (proposed) may REQUIRE a route: `route=\\\"COMMIT\\\"` turns a PASTE into `ISSUE`.\\n    72\\tH2. **The content verdict is exact.** `dictate_emulator(sentence, target_package, expect=None)`: the expected editor text is `before_text + expect`, where `expect` defaults to the literal rendering rule of a plain sentence, `sentence[:1].upper() + sentence[1:] + \\\".\\\"` (written here as a literal, not computed by the app; if the app's cleanup changes, this goes red loudly and the caller passes `expect`). The line is `VERIFIED: the same editor's whole text now equals the expectation (N chars)` or `ISSUE: the editor's whole text differs from the expectation; it ends …`. `debug_insert(text)` compares with `before_text + text`. `_sentence_landed` is deleted (its only callers were these two); `_plain` stays for `find`.\\n    73\\tH3. **Only a uniquely focused editor is a target.** `_focused_field`: `chosen = [n for n in fields if n[\\\"focused\\\"]]`; none → `None`; more than one → `Blocked(\\\"N editors are focused …\\\")`. `focus_field` already reads back focus.\\n    74\\tH4. **`bound()` reads the whole block.** `re.search(r\\\"Bound services:\\\\{(.*)\\\\}\\\\s*$\\\", out, re.M)` then `\\\"label=EnviousWispr\\\" in block`; a missing block stays `Blocked`.\\n    75\\tH5. **Evidence is bounded to the owned take.** `clear_log()` records the device clock (`date '+%m-%d %H:%M:%S.000'`) in `_STATE[\\\"log_since\\\"]` (proposed key); `last_take()`, `recording()` and `_wait_for_the_take_to_finish` read `logcat -d -T '<since>'` when it is set and the WHOLE buffer with `\\\"bounded\\\": False` in the result when it is not; `last_take()` requires exactly one `recording_start` in the window, else `{\\\"unknown\\\": \\\"N takes in the window\\\"}` and the callers report `ISSUE: … UNKNOWN`.\\n    76\\tH6. **Recording off is `NOT RUN`.** Every report-returning `_recording_is_off()` caller returns `NOT RUN: {RECORDING_IS_OFF}` before staging (four suites, §10); the guard's own two raises inside `open_recorder` stay; `RECORDING_IS_OFF` text unchanged.\\n    77\\tH7. **The book is keyed by hardware identity.** `_book_key()` (proposed) = `ro.serialno` read once per `device()` into `_STATE[\\\"identity\\\"]` (the transport serial kept in `_STATE[\\\"serial\\\"]`); `_owe_locked`, `_owed`, `_settled_locked` and `restore()` use `_book_key()`; on first read under the lock, entries under the current transport serial are MOVED under the identity key (migration, never a drop). `restore()` reports which key it paid. `host` stays `host`.\\n    78\\tH8. **An owned screen recording.** `screen_recording(path)` (proposed) context manager: journals `(\\\"screenrecord\\\", pid_or_marker)` BEFORE `adb shell screenrecord --time-limit 180 /sdcard/wispr-eyes/<token>.mp4` starts (background), stops it with `kill -2 <pid>` found by `pidof screenrecord` (refuses when more than one), waits for the file to stop growing, pulls it to `path`, deletes the device file, settles the debt; End-to-end state and lifecycle audit\\n   104\\tAsync edges for the device rows (`code-design-rules.md` RULE: async-edge-case-enumeration): Interrupted (the driver dies before injecting: the take ends by the 3 s silence bound or the cap; the test's 90 s wait names the phase seen; `restore()` pays the journal) · Deleted (the receipt file removed mid-run: the read fails loudly, not as `\\\"\\\"`, because the row asserts the file EXISTS then its text) · Mutated (a second take writes the receipt: `count(EXPECTED) == 1` fails) · Concurrent (two instrumentation runs: `am instrument` serialises per runner; the harness refuses when `pidof` shows one running) · Absent (no History row within the bound: the failure names the rows seen; fail closed) · Stale (an old row: the row awaited must be CREATED after the test's start timestamp, read from `createdAtMs`).\\n   105\\tFor the harness: the `log_since` (proposed) key unset → `bounded: False` in the result and the verdict says so; a journal migration racing another session → under `_journal_locked`, first-writer moves, second finds nothing to move.\\n   106\\t\\n   107\\t## 6. Only the founder can flip that switch. |\\n    30\\t| Is the port normalised? | `adb connect 100.94.206.47:5555` from the Mac | After a reboot the port is random again: `adb connect localhost:<port> && adb tcpip 5555 && adb connect localhost:5555`. |\\n    31\\t\\n    32\\t`getprop init.svc.adbd` and `sys.usb.config` read as if they answer this and do not.\\n    33\\t\\n    34\\t`android-bridge/adb-recover.sh` automates the port loop and must run ON THE PHONE\\n    35\\t(`ssh -p 8022 u0_a517@100.94.206.47 'bash ~/android-bridge/adb-recover.sh'`); on the Mac it fails on a\\n    36\\tmissing log path and a WiFi check. Match the\\n    43\\tserial: `adb devices | grep -qE \\\"^100\\\\.94\\\\.206\\\\.47:5555[[:space:]]+device$\\\"`, with a control that the\\n    44\\tpattern does NOT match while only the emulator is up.\\n    45\\t\\n    46\\t## RULE: connectedAndroidTest-UNINSTALLS-the-app-so-never-point-it-at-the-daily-phone\\n    47\\t`./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest` installs both APKs, runs, and UNINSTALLS them on the way out,\\n    48\\ttaking app-private storage with it: both models, the history, the custom words, every hand-granted\\n    49\\tpermission and the saved settings, so ONBOARDING RETURNS. `scripts/hooks/command-safety.py` denies any\\n    50\\tGradle task named `connected*` and prints the `am instrument` form; an `ANDROID_SERIAL=emulator-*` target\\n    51\\tstill runs.\\n    52\\t\\n    53\\tThe symptom after the fact is `run-as: unknown package`, `pm path` printing nothing, or `am start`\\n    54\\tanswering `Activity class ... does not exist`. Storage and Keystore suites ask nothing of the microphone, NPU, side button or a real editor: run\\n    78\\tthem on `emulator-5554`.\\n    79\\t\\n    80\\t## RULE: drive-the-instrumented-tests-with-am-instrument-not-gradle\\n    81\\t`am instrument` does not uninstall, so it is the way to run a device test against the founder's phone:\\n    82\\t\\n    83\\t```bash\\n    84\\tADB=~/Android/sdk/platform-tools/adb\\n    85\\tD=100.94.206.47:5555\\n    86\\t./gradlew :app:assembleDebug :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest\\n    87\\t$ADB -s $D install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk\\n    88\\t$ADB -s $D install -r -t app/build/outputs/apk/androidTest/debug/app-debug-androidTest.apk   # -t: test-only\\n    89\\t$ADB -s $D shell 'am instrument -w -e class com.envi.wispr.VoicePipelineDeviceTest#<method> \\\\\\n    90\\t    com.envi.wispr.test/androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner'\\n    91\\t```\\n    92\\t\\n    93\\t- **Re-enable accessibility after EVERY `install -r`** (it unbinds the service and clears\\n    94\\t  `enabled_accessibility_services`); set it back, wait a few seconds, never in the same breath as the install.\\n    95\\t- **Generate the spoken audio with Azure Speech** (`~/.claude/knowledge/ai/cloud-llm-credits.md`, voice\\n    96\\t  `en-US-AvaNeural`, `X-Microsoft-OutputFormat: raw-16khz-16bit-mono-pcm` is exactly the headerless\\n    97\\t  fixture format). History shows the transcript and NO status line.\\n   580\\t\\n   581\\t**Unclean-stop marker, a separate run:** `$ADB shell am crash com.envi.wispr`, relaunch, `$ADB logcat -d |\\n   582\\tgrep 'Reconnected after an unclean stop'`; repeat after an off-and-on cycle in Accessibility settings, where\\n   583\\tits absence is the `MIN-1` regression.\\n   584\\t\\n   585\\t**Two silences are part of the acceptance:** a user who never granted the permission (disable, dictate,\\n   586\\twords land on the clipboard, nothing else); and a dictation with no field (service bound, dictate from the\\n   587\\ttile: `$ADB logcat -d | grep 'handoff='` reads `NO_PINNED_TARGET`, shade empty).\\n   588\\t\\n   589\\t## FACT: the-issue-16-state-cannot-be-staged-by-settings\\n   590\\t**Measured on the S26, 2026-08-30, running the `fix/16-auto-paste-readiness` build.**\\n   591\\t\\n   592\\tThe state issue #16 describes is `Enabled services` naming us while the service is DEAD: permission TRUE,\\n   593\\tbinding FALSE. **No settings lever reaches it on Android 16.**\\n   594\\t\\n   595\\t- `settings put secure accessibility_enabled 0` does not unbind at all.\\n   596\\t- `settings delete secure enabled_accessibility_services` unbinds, but it also revokes the permission, so\\n   597\\t  the app correctly classifies the result as NOT_PERMITTED — a user who never granted it — and stays\\n   598\\t  silent by design.\\n   599\\t- Turning the service off in Accessibility settings does the same thing by hand.\\n   600\\t\\n   601\\t**Only a genuine service crash produces permission-true-and-unbound**, which is what the founder saw and\\n   602\\twhat `Crashed services` reported. So a UAT that deletes the setting proves the clipboard fallback and the\\n   603\\tNOT_PERMITTED silence, and CANNOT prove the message a permitted-but-dead user gets.\\n   604\\t\\n   605\\t**What this means for anyone testing #16:** the readiness half is provable, the announcement half is not,\\n   606\\tuntil the service can be crashed on demand. The unclean-stop marker is the nearest instrument.\\n   607\\t\\n   608\\t## FACT: what-the-2026-08-30-run-actually-proved\\n   609\\tEnd to end on the phone, with the `fix/16-auto-paste-readiness` build installed:\\n   610\\t\\n   611\\t- **Auto-paste alive:** dictation reached the Messages compose field. `Insertion completed via SET_TEXT\\n   612\\t  after 1 attempt(s)`, `handoff=SCHEDULED`, and the polished sentence was visible in the field with cleanup\\n   613\\t  punctuation applied.\\n   614\\t- **Auto-paste unbound:** `handoff=SERVICE_NOT_RUNNING`, the transcript reached the clipboard, and pasting\\n   615\\t  it into a fresh field returned the text. The clipboard fallback works.\\n   616\\t- **The app stayed silent**, correctly, because the same lever that unbinds also revokes, so the state it\\n   617\\t  saw was NOT_PERMITTED.
