Everything else — checking the test package, reading and lowering the media volume,\n3474:    _, will_say = stage_phone_speech(sentence, volume=volume, use_fixture=use_fixture)\n3479:    playing = will_say[\"seconds\"]\n3481:    report.append(f\"NOTE: the phone will play {will_say['what']}\"\n3516:    # THE OUTCOME, not the request. `handoff=SCHEDULED` says the text was handed over; only the\n3517:    # editor's own content says it arrived. Measured 2026-09-06: a run logged SCHEDULED and then\n3525:        report.append(\"ISSUE: a DIFFERENT editor is on screen now, so nothing here says where the words \"\n  2500\t        raise Blocked(f\"{pcm_path} is not a file\")\n  2501\t    if not recording():\n  2502\t        raise Blocked(\"no take is listening on the emulator, so injected audio would be dropped. \"\n  2503\t                      \"Inject inside `with open_recorder():`.\")\n  2504\t    packets = pcm_path + \".packets.jsonl\"\n  2505\t    count, seconds = _audio_packets(pcm_path, packets)\n  2506\t    _grpc(\"injectAudio\", stdin_path=packets, timeout=int(seconds) + 60)\n  2507\t    return f\"injected {count} packets, {seconds:.1f}s of audio\"\n  2508\t\n  2509\t\n  2510\tdef _focused_field(target_package):\n  2511\t    \"\"\"The one focused editor in the target app, as (package, identity, text); None when there is none.\n  2512\t\n  2513\t    IDENTITY TRAVELS WITH THE TEXT so a before/after comparison is about ONE editor. Exactly one FOCUSED\n  2514\t    editor is required: an unfocused field can become \"the target\" and read as words having arrived\n  2515\t    somewhere they were never aimed (#161).\n  2516\t    \"\"\"\n  2517\t    fields = [n for n in tree(refresh=True) if n[\"kind\"] == \"EditText\"\n  2518\t              and (target_package is None or n[\"package\"] == target_package)\n  2519\t              and n[\"focused\"]]\n  2520\t    if not fields:\n  2521\t        return None\n  2522\t    if len(fields) > 1:\n  2523\t        raise Blocked(f\"{len(fields)} focused editors are on screen, so which one the words were \"\n  2524\t                      \"meant for is a guess\")\n  2525\t    node = fields[0]\n  2526\t    return (node[\"package\"], node[\"id\"] or node[\"bounds\"], node[\"text\"])\n  2527\t\n  2528\t\n  2529\tdef _plain(text):\n  2530\t    \"\"\"A text with only the app's own decoration removed: NFKC, case-folded, punctuation dropped,\n  2531\t    whitespace collapsed. NOT a tokenizer: three review rounds each found a script a tokenizer broke\n  2532\t    (Cyrillic, combining marks, unspaced CJK), so the verdict is a plain substring match on this.\"\"\"\n  2533\t    import unicodedata\n  2534\t    folded = unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKC\", text or \"\").casefold()\n  2535\t    kept = \"\".join(c for c in folded if not unicodedata.category(c).startswith(\"P\"))\n  2536\t    return \" \".join(kept.split())\n  2537\t\n  2538\t\n  2539\tdef _sentence_landed(sentence, text):\n  2540\t    \"\"\"Whether the sentence appears in the text, exactly, once case, punctuation and spacing are aside.\n  2541\t\n  2542\t    Word membership alone passed \"beta alpha\" for \"alpha beta\" (review round 1, 2026-09-20); a word\n  2543\t    tokenizer then failed Cyrillic, then combining marks and unspaced CJK (rounds 2 and 3), so this is a\n  2544\t    substring match on `_plain`, which splits nothing.\n  2545\t    \"\"\"\n  2546\t    # THE APP CAPITALISES THE FIRST LETTER, and case folding is not a bijection: Turkish `ı` folds\n  2547\t    # differently from the `I` the app writes (review round 4), so the capitalised form is tried too.\n  2548\t    got = _plain(text)\n  2549\t    variants = {_plain(sentence), _plain(sentence[:1].upper() + sentence[1:])}\n  2550\t    return any(wanted and wanted in got for wanted in variants)\n  2551\t\n  2552\t\n  2553\tdef _excerpt(text, keep=80):\n  2554\t    \"\"\"The tail of an editor's text, so a report line stays one line whatever the draft has grown to.\"\"\"\n  2555\t    text = (text or \"\").replace(\"\\xa0\", \" \").strip()\n  2556\t    return repr(text if len(text) <= keep else \"…\" + text[-keep:]) + f\" ({len(text)} chars)\"\n  2557\t\n  2558\t\n  2559\tdef open_app(package):\n  2560\t    \"\"\"Bring an app to the front by its package, the way the launcher would, and assert it arrived.\"\"\"\n  2561\t    ready()\n  2562\t    _adb(f\"monkey -p {shlex.quote(package)} -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1\")\n  2563\t    for _ in range(8):\n  2564\t        time.sleep(0.5)\n  2565\t        _STATE[\"tree\"] = None\n  2566\t        if package in {n[\"package\"] for n in tree()}:\n  2567\t            return f\"{package} is on screen\"\n  2568\t    raise Blocked(f\"{package} did not come to the front\")\n  2569\t\n  2570\t\n  2571\tdef focus_field(label, package):\n  2572\t    \"\"\"Press an editor by its hint or text and READ BACK that it took focus.\n  2573\t\n  2574\t    An editor is pressable by definition, whatever the tree says about `clickable`, so the press lands\n  2575\t    on the label's own centre. The read-back is the point: a dictation aims at the focused field, and a\n  2576\t    press that did not focus it would send the words somewhere else.\n  2577\t    \"\"\"\n  2578\t    tap(label, clickable=False, package=package)\n  2579\t    time.sleep(0.8)\n  2580\t    field = _focused_field(package)\n  2581\t    if field is None:\n  2582\t        raise Blocked(f\"{label!r} was pressed but no editor in {package} has focus\")\n  2583\t    return f\"focused {label!r} ({field[1]})\"\n  2584\t\n  2585\t\n  2586\tdef dictate_emulator(sentence=\"and I will send the deck tomorrow\", target_package=\"com.google.android.gm\"):\n  2587\t    \"\"\"One spoken take on the EMULATOR, fed over gRPC, judged by the editor's own text.\n  2588\t\n  2589\t    Replaces `scripts/uat/grpc-take.sh`, which tapped coordinates it had worked out by hand, turned the\n  2590\t    host microphone off and never back on, and trusted a log line. Here the take is owned by\n  2591\t    `open_recorder()`, the microphone by `set_host_mic()` and its journal, and the verdict by the field\n  2592\t    that was focused before the take and is still the same field after it.\n  2593\t    \"\"\"\n  2594\t    _require_emulator(\"a spoken take\")\n  2595\t    if _recording_is_off():\n  2596\t        return [f\"BLOCKED: {RECORDING_IS_OFF}\"]\n  2597\t    report = []\n  2598\t    restore()\n  2599\t    ready()\n  2600\t    if not bound():\n  2601\t        return [\"BLOCKED: auto-paste is switched off, so nothing can be inserted. \"\n  2602\t                \"enable_auto_paste() turns it back on.\"]\n  2603\t    before = _focused_field(target_package)\n  2604\t    if before is None:\n  2605\t        return [f\"BLOCKED: no focused editor in {target_package} is on screen; tap into one first\"]\n  2606\t    scratch = os.path.join(os.environ.get(\"TMPDIR\", \"/tmp\"), \"wispr-eyes\")\n  2607\t    os.makedirs(scratch, exist_ok=True)\n  2608\t    pcm = _pcm_from_sentence(sentence, os.path.join(scratch, f\"utt-{uuid.uuid4().hex}.pcm\"))\n  2609\t    report.append(f\"NOTE: {sentence!r} was rendered to {pcm}\")\n  2610\t    ending = None\n  2611\t    try:\n  2612\t        # OFF AS THE RESTING STATE, never a switch inside the take: see _rest_host_mic_off. Done before\n  2613\t        # the audio is rendered so the switch, if one happens at all, is as far from the capture as the\n  2614\t        # call allows.\n  2615\t        report.append(f\"NOTE: {_rest_host_mic_off()}\")\n  2616\t        clear_log()\n  2617\t        with open_recorder(verify=False):\n  2618\t            time.sleep(3.0)  # the recogniser warms; injecting sooner is dropped (grpc-take.sh, 2026-09-13)\n  2619\t            report.append(f\"NOTE: {inject_audio(pcm)}\")\n  2620\t            time.sleep(2.0)\n  2621\t            stop_dictation()\n  2622\t            ending = _wait_for_the_take_to_finish()\n  2623\t    finally:\n  2624\t        for line in restore():\n  2625\t            report.append(f\"NOTE: restored {line}\")\n  2626\t    if ending is None:\n  2627\t        report.append(\"ISSUE: the dictation never reached an ending, so nothing can be said about it\")\n  2628\t        return report\n  2629\t    take = last_take()\n  2630\t    report.append(f\"VERIFIED: a take ran, ended by {take['ended_by']}\" if take[\"ended_by\"]\n  2631\t                  else \"ISSUE: no take ending was logged\")\n  2632\t    if take[\"transcribed_chars\"]:\n  2633\t        report.append(f\"VERIFIED: {take['transcribed_chars']} characters came back from the speech engine\")\n  2634\t    else:\n  2635\t        report.append(\"ISSUE: nothing was transcribed; either the stream never reached the microphone \"\n  2636\t                      \"or the engine returned empty\")\n  2637\t    _, route = _adb(\"logcat -d | grep 'insertion api=' | grep -v adbd | tail -1\", check=False)\n  2638\t    if route.strip():\n  2639\t        report.append(f\"NOTE: {route.strip()[-160:]}\")\n  2640\t    after = _focused_field(target_package)\n  2641\t    if after is None:\n  2642\t        report.append(\"ISSUE: no focused editor is on screen after the take, so where the words went \"\n  2643\t                      \"is unknown\")\n  2644\t    elif after[:2] != before[:2]:\n  2645\t        report.append(\"ISSUE: a DIFFERENT editor is focused now, so nothing here says where the words went\")\n  2646\t    elif after[2] == before[2]:\n  2647\t        report.append(f\"ISSUE: the editor is unchanged; it still holds {after[2]!r}\")\n  2648\t    else:\n  2649\t        if not _sentence_landed(sentence, after[2]):\n  2650\t            report.append(f\"ISSUE: the editor changed but does not hold the sentence in order; it ends \"\n  2651\t                          f\"{_excerpt(after[2])}\")\n  2652\t        else:\n  2653\t            report.append(f\"VERIFIED: the same editor now holds the sentence; it ends {_excerpt(after[2])}\")\n  2654\t    return report\n  2655\t\n  2656\t\n  2657\tdef debug_insert(text, target_package=None):\n  2658\t    \"\"\"Insert a sentence through the app's real insertion path with NO audio, on the EMULATOR's DEBUG build.\n  2659\t\n  2660\t    Replaces `scripts/uat/debug-insert.sh`. The debug-only broadcast pins the focused editor and\n  2661\t    commits or pastes exactly as a take would, so it drives the caret matrix deterministically. The\n  2662\t    editor's own text is the verdict, never the clipboard.\n  2663\t    \"\"\"\n  2664\t    _require_emulator(\"the debug insert\")\n  2665\t    ready()\n  2666\t    if not bound():\n  2667\t        return [\"BLOCKED: auto-paste is switched off, so nothing can be inserted\"]\n  2668\t    # THE PACKAGE's flag line is the bracketed one; the first bare `flags=0x0` belongs to a component\n  2669\t    # and read as \"not debuggable\" on the first live run (2026-09-20).\n  2670\t    _, dump = _adb(f\"dumpsys package {PACKAGE} | grep -m1 DEBUGGABLE\", check=False)\n  2671\t    if \"DEBUGGABLE\" not in dump:\n  2672\t        return [f\"BLOCKED: the installed {PACKAGE} is not a debug build, so the insert receiver is absent\"]\n  2673\t    before = _focused_field(target_package)\n  2674\t    if before is None:\n  2675\t        return [\"BLOCKED: no focused editor is on screen; tap into one first\"]\n  2676\t    clear_log()\n  2677\t    _adb(f\"am broadcast -a {PACKAGE}.debug.INSERT --es text {shlex.quote(text)} {PACKAGE}\")\n  2678\t    time.sleep(4)\n  2679\t    report = []\n  2680\t    # `grep -v adbd`: adbd logs the shell command it was asked to run, pattern included, so without it\n  2681\t    # the last line read back is this very grep.\n  2682\t    _, lines = _adb(\"logcat -d | grep -E 'insertion api=|DebugInsert: pin=' | grep -v adbd | tail -2\",\n  2683\t                    check=False)\n  2684\t    for line in lines.strip().splitlines():\n  2685\t        report.append(f\"NOTE: {line.strip()[-160:]}\")\n  2686\t    after = _focused_field(target_package)\n  2687\t    if after is None or after[:2] != before[:2]:\n  2688\t        report.append(\"ISSUE: the focused editor changed or vanished, so where the text went is unknown\")\n  2689\t    elif text in (after[2] or \"\"):\n  2690\t        report.append(f\"VERIFIED: the same editor now holds the text; it ends {_excerpt(after[2])}\")\n  2691\t    else:\n  2692\t        report.append(f\"ISSUE: the editor reads {after[2]!r}, which does not contain {text!r}\")\n  2693\t    return report\n  2694\t\n  2695\t\n  2696\tdef open_page(url, package=\"com.android.chrome\"):\n  2697\t    \"\"\"Open a URL in a browser and assert the browser is on screen. Nothing is sent to anyone.\"\"\"\n  2698\t    ready()\n  2699\t    remote, out = _adb(f\"am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d {shlex.quote(url)} {shlex.quote(package)}\",\n  2700\t                       check=False)\n  2701\t    if remote != 0 or \"Error\" in out:\n  2702\t        detail = out.strip().splitlines()[-1] if out.strip() else \"no message\"\n  2703\t        raise Blocked(f\"{url} would not open in {package}: {detail}\")\n  2704\t    for _ in range(6):\n  2705\t        time.sleep(0.5)\n  2706\t        _STATE[\"tree\"] = None\n  2707\t        if package in {n[\"package\"] for n in tree()}:\n  2708\t            return f\"{package} is showing {url}\"\n  2709\t    raise Blocked(f\"{package} did not come to the front for {url}\")\n  2710\t\n  2800\t        started = time.monotonic()\n  2801\t        _checked([\"say\", \"-v\", \"Samantha\", \"-r\", \"170\", \"-a\", CABLE, \"--\", sentence], timeout=180)\n  2802\t        return time.monotonic() - started\n  2803\t    finally:\n  2804\t        # BOTH cleanups run whatever the other does: the Mac's input goes back, and the emulator's host\n  2805\t        # mic returns to its OFF resting state (#181; the on-debt `set_host_mic(True)` wrote is settled\n  2806\t        # by that, or kept for `restore()` if the switch fails).\n  2807\t        try:\n  2808\t            _restore_one(entry)\n  2809\t            _settled(entry, serial=\"host\")\n  2810\t        finally:\n  2811\t            _rest_host_mic_off()\n  2812\t\n  2813\t\n  2814\t@_atomic_change\n  2815\tdef say(sentence, volume=25):\n  2816\t    \"\"\"Speak a sentence out of the MAC's speakers, into the phone's microphone, quietly.\n  2817\t\n  2818\t    The Mac speaks rather than the phone, so the phone's own audio settings are never touched and the\n  2819\t    sound arrives through the air like a person talking. The founder's standing instruction is that any\n  2820\t    audio test runs at LOW VOLUME.\n  2821\t\n  2822\t    The volume is put back in a `finally` and then READ BACK. Restoring in the happy path only is how a\n  2823\t    timeout leaves a machine loud, and trusting a restore nobody checked is how it stays loud quietly.\n  2824\t\n  2825\t    **The phone has to be near the Mac.** That is the one precondition this cannot check, so a report\n  2826\t    says it rather than assuming it.\n  2827\t\n  2828\t    **On an emulator the voice goes through the cable instead** ([say_into_emulator]): `say_on_phone`\n  2829\t    plays through the guest speaker, which no guest microphone hears, and the speaker-to-microphone\n  2830\t    path was the flaky half of every emulator take.\n  2831\t    \"\"\"\n  2832\t    if not isinstance(volume, int) or isinstance(volume, bool) or not 0 <= volume <= 40:\n  2833\t        raise Blocked(\"volume must be a whole number from 0 to 40; this is a low-volume tool\")\n  2834\t    if is_emulator():\n  2835\t        return say_into_emulator(sentence)\n  2836\t    previous = _checked([\"osascript\", \"-e\", \"output volume of (get volume settings)\"]).strip()\n  2837\t    if not previous.isdigit():\n  2838\t        raise Blocked(\"could not read the Mac's current volume, so it could not be safely lowered\")\n  2839\t    entry = (\"mac-volume\", previous)\n  2840\t    # Written BEFORE the change, and scoped to the HOST rather than to a phone: the Mac's speakers are\n  2841\t    # not a setting on anybody's device, and filing them under a serial would make them restorable only\n  2842\t    # while that phone is the one being driven.\n  2843\t    _owe(entry, serial=\"host\")\n  2844\t    try:\n  2845\t        _checked([\"osascript\", \"-e\", f\"set volume output volume {volume}\"])\n  2846\t        started = time.monotonic()\n  2847\t        _checked([\"say\", \"--\", sentence], timeout=180)\n  2848\t        return time.monotonic() - started\n  2849\t    finally:\n  2850\t        _restore_one(entry)\n  2851\t        _settled(entry, serial=\"host\")\n  2852\t\n  2853\t\n  2854\t# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n  2855\t# Reading what happened\n  2856\t# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n  2857\t\n  2858\tdef clear_log():\n  2859\t    \"\"\"Clear the ring buffer so an absent line means absent rather than left over.\n  2860\t\n  2861\t    **IT CHANGES THE PHONE AND CANNOT BE PUT BACK, and that is stated rather than journaled.** The log\n  2862\t    it discards is gone; a debt promising to restore it would be a lie, and a lie in the restore book is\n  2863\t    worse than an honest gap. What is lost is diagnostic history, never the founder's own data.\n  2864\t\n  2865\t    **It no longer RESIZES the buffer, and that is a deletion rather than a fix.** The old version\n  2866\t    widened it to 16M and journaled \"the buffer was N K\" from the first line of `logcat -g` — which\n  2867\t    names one buffer out of several, and silently journaled nothing at all when that line did not match,\n  2868\t    while still doing the resize. A debt that cannot describe the change it undoes is worse than no\n  2869\t    resize: it leaves the founder's phone altered and the book saying otherwise. Every take this tool\n  2870\t    measures is seconds long, so the default buffer holds it.\n  2871\t    \"\"\"\n  2872\t    _adb(\"logcat -c\")\n  2873\t\n  2874\t\n  2875\tdef keep_awake(minutes=30):\n  3100\t    elif what == \"host-mic\":\n  3101\t        wanted = previous == \"on\"\n  3102\t        _grpc(\"setMicrophoneState\", {\"realAudioEnabled\": wanted})\n  3103\t        now = _mic_state()\n  3104\t        if now != wanted:\n  3105\t            raise Blocked(f\"the emulator's host microphone did not go back {previous}; it reads \"\n  3106\t                          f\"{'on' if now else 'off'}\")\n  3107\t    elif what == \"frozen-process\":\n  3108\t        _thaw(json.loads(previous))\n  3109\t    elif what == \"screen-timeout\":\n  3110\t        _adb(f\"settings put system screen_off_timeout {int(previous)}\")\n  3111\t        _, now = _adb(\"settings get system screen_off_timeout\")\n  3112\t        if now.strip() != str(int(previous)):\n  3113\t            raise Blocked(f\"the screen timeout did not go back to {previous}; it reads {now.strip()}\")\n  3114\t    else:\n  3115\t        raise Blocked(f\"there is no verified way to put {what!r} back, so it must not have been journaled\")\n  3116\t\n  3117\t\n  3118\tdef restore():\n  3119\t    \"\"\"Put back everything this session changed, and say what.\n  3120\t\n  3121\t    **THE WHOLE RUN IS UNDER THE BOOK'S LOCK, and that is the fix for the last race.** Reading the book,\n  3122\t    acting on it, and settling were three separate steps with gaps between them, so another session could\n  3123\t    decide what to do from a state that had already changed: it read a take debt, checked and found\n  3124\t    nothing recording YET, waited, and then erased the debt of a recording that had started in the\n  3125\t    meantime. Deciding and settling have to be one indivisible act.\n  3126\t    \"\"\"\n  3127\t    with _journal_locked():\n  3128\t        return _restore_locked()\n  3129\t\n  3130\t\n  3131\tdef _restore_locked():\n  3132\t    \"\"\"Put back everything this session changed, and say what.\n  3133\t\n  3134\t    An entry is removed ONLY after its restore was read back. A failure leaves it in the journal and\n  3135\t    raises, so the next call tries again rather than reporting a rollback that did not happen.\n  3136\t\n  3137\t    **What this does NOT cover, said plainly rather than implied:** a dictation this tool started and\n  3138\t    the History row it produced, the app's foreground state, and onboarding once dismissed. Those are\n  3139\t    dev state on a phone with no users (`CLAUDE.md`: a wiped phone is cheap), but they are not restored\n  3140\t    and no report should say they were.\n  3141\t    \"\"\"\n  3142\t    _STATE[\"restored_for\"] = None\n  3143\t    done = []\n  3144\t    # The HOST book first, then this device's, then any OTHER device in the book that is attached right\n  3145\t    # now. A debt owed to a device that is not attached cannot be verified, so it is reported and kept,\n  3146\t    # never settled: an unverified restore is not a restore. The other attached devices are driven\n  3147\t    # through `_as_serial`, so the selection this process made is untouched afterwards.\n  3148\t    selected = device()\n  3149\t    attached = {serial for serial, _ in devices()}\n  3150\t    others = sorted(scope for scope in _journal_read() if scope not in (\"host\", selected))\n  3151\t    for scope in [\"host\", selected] + others:\n  3152\t        if scope not in (\"host\", selected) and scope not in attached:\n  3153\t            if _owed(scope):\n  3154\t                done.append(f\"{scope}: not attached, debt kept\")\n  3155\t            continue\n  3156\t        for entry in list(_owed(scope)):\n  3157\t            _restore_one(entry, serial=None if scope in (\"host\", selected) else scope)\n  3158\t            _settled_locked(entry, scope)\n  3159\t            done.append(f\"{entry[0]} back to {entry[1]}\" + (\"\" if scope in (\"host\", selected) else f\" on {scope}\"))\n  3160\t    _STATE[\"restore\"] = []\n  3161\t    # THE SCREEN DUMP IS NOT DELETED, and that is the whole of it. `rm -f` on a fixed path removes\n  3162\t    # whatever is sitting there, and \"it looks like XML\" is a description, not proof of ownership: a\n  3163\t    # file of the founder's with that name and that shape would go silently. It is one small file that\n  3164\t    # every run overwrites, so leaving it costs nothing and deleting it can cost something that is not\n  3165\t    # ours to spend.\n  3166\t    _STATE[\"restored_for\"] = device()\n  3167\t    return done or [\"nothing was changed\"]\n  3168\t\n  3169\t\n  3170\t# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n  3171\t# Suites, each answering one question end to end\n  3172\t# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n  3173\t\n  3174\tdef check_recorder():\n  3175\t    \"\"\"Does the floating recorder open, and can the user see it? One call, and it always tidies up.\"\"\"\n  3176\t    if _recording_is_off():\n  3177\t        return [f\"BLOCKED: {RECORDING_IS_OFF}\"]\n  3178\t    ready()\n  3179\t    report = []\n  3180\t    # The phone is left clean before anything is recorded on it, which is also what makes the take\n  3181\t    # below allowed to start at all.\n  3182\t    report.append(\"put back first: \" + \"; \".join(restore()))\n  3183\t    if not bound():\n  3184\t        return [\"BLOCKED: auto-paste is switched off, so no recorder will be drawn. \"\n  3185\t                \"enable_auto_paste() turns it back on.\"]\n  3186\t    clear_log()\n  3187\t    try:\n  3188\t        with open_recorder() as pill:\n  3189\t            report.append(\n  3190\t                f\"VERIFIED: the recorder is on screen at {pill['where']}, \"\n  3191\t                f\"{pill['size'][0]}x{pill['size'][1]}\")\n  3192\t            report.append(\"VERIFIED: a take is running\" if recording()\n  3193\t                          else \"ISSUE: the recorder is drawn but nothing is recording\")\n  3194\t    except Blocked as why:\n  3195\t        report.append(f\"ISSUE: {why}\")\n  3196\t    # AFTER the block, so this is asking whether the context manager's own cleanup worked.\n  3197\t    time.sleep(1.5)\n  3198\t    try:\n  3199\t        report.append(\"ISSUE: the take would not cancel and is STILL RECORDING\" if recording()\n  3200\t                      else \"VERIFIED: the take was cancelled and nothing is listening\")\n  3201\t    except Blocked as why:\n  3202\t        report.append(f\"ISSUE: whether anything is still recording could not be read: {why}\")\n  3203\t    return report\n  3204\t\n  3205\t\n  3206\t# The lines that END a dictation, whatever the outcome. Polling for one of these is how\n  3207\t# `scripts/uat/dictate-once.sh` decides a run is over, and it beats a fixed sleep in both directions:\n  3208\t# a slow take is not cut off, and a fast one does not cost fourteen seconds of nothing.\n  3209\t# How long the recorder waits before the audio starts, and after it ends. Both are the smallest value\n  3210\t# that worked rather than a comfortable one: the lead-in covers the speaker activity launching, and the\n  3211\t# trailing margin covers the last word reaching the microphone. Everything beyond them is the founder\n  3212\t# watching his own recorder run on silence.\n  3213\tLEAD_IN_S = 1.5\n  3214\tTRAILING_MARGIN_S = 1.0\n  3215\t\n  3216\t_TERMINAL_LINES = (\n  3217\t    \"Auto-insert handed\", \"kept on clipboard\", \"Transcription failed\",\n  3218\t    \"Speech recognition failed\", \"No audio captured\", \"showError\",\n  3219\t    # `Take terminal: <STATE>` is the session's own ending line (seen `NO_SPEECH` on 2026-09-20); without\n  3220\t    # it a take that heard nothing waited the full 40 s and 200 log reads before saying so.\n  3221\t    \"Take terminal:\",\n  3222\t)\n  3223\t\n  3224\t\n  3225\tdef _wait_for_the_take_to_finish(seconds=40):\n  3226\t    \"\"\"Poll the log until the dictation reaches an ending, and say which one. None on a timeout.\"\"\"\n  3227\t    for _ in range(seconds * 2):\n  3228\t        time.sleep(0.5)\n  3229\t        text = logs(lines=200)\n  3230\t        for marker in _TERMINAL_LINES:\n  3231\t            if marker in text:\n  3232\t                return marker\n  3233\t    return None\n  3234\t\n  3235\t\n  3236\t# THE WHOLE APP, AS IT IS ON SCREEN. Walked by hand on 2026-09-06 and checked against the code that\n  3237\t# produces it: `AppShell.kt`'s `AppDestination` for the four tabs and `SettingsPage` for the eight\n  3238\t# drawer pages, so a page added to the app and not to this list is a gap somebody can find rather than\n  3239\t# an invisible one. `scan()` reports any page it meets that is not named here.\n  3240\tTABS = (\"History\", \"Dictionary\", \"Transcription\", \"AI Polish\")\n  3241\tPAGES = (\"What's New\", \"Appearance\", \"Microphone\", \"Sounds\", \"Clipboard\",\n  3242\t         \"Permissions\", \"Privacy\", \"Storage\", \"Open Source Licenses\")\n  3243\t\n  3244\t\n  3245\tdef _tab_row(package=PACKAGE):\n  3246\t    \"\"\"The four tab labels along the bottom, found by the ONLY thing that distinguishes them.\n  3247\t\n  3248\t    **Every tab name is on screen TWICE**: once as the heading of the page you are on, and once in the\n  3249\t    tab bar. `find('History')` correctly refuses that as ambiguous, so something has to say which is\n  3250\t    which, and it must not be a coordinate somebody typed.\n  3251\t\n  3252\t    The rule is structural: the tab bar is the one horizontal band that holds ALL FOUR names. A heading\n  3253\t    is alone in its band. So the band is found by asking the app where its own four labels agree,\n  3254\t    which survives a different phone, a different text size and a moved bar.\n  3255\t    \"\"\"\n  3256\t    nodes = [n for n in tree(refresh=False) if n[\"package\"] == package and _label(n) in TABS]\n  3257\t    for candidate in nodes:\n  3258\t        top, bottom = candidate[\"bounds\"][1], candidate[\"bounds\"][3]\n  3259\t        band = [n for n in nodes if n[\"bounds\"][1] < bottom and n[\"bounds\"][3] > top]\n  3260\t        if len({_label(n) for n in band}) == len(TABS):\n  3261\t            return {_label(n): n for n in band}\n  3262\t    raise Blocked(\n  3263\t        \"the four tabs are not all on screen, so which label is the tab bar cannot be told from which \"\n  3264\t        \"is a page heading. What is there:\\n\" + look(only_ours=True)\n  3265\t    )\n  3360\t                    report.append(f\"ISSUE: {name} / {label}: {why}\")\n  3361\t                    continue\n  3362\t                report.append(\n  3363\t                    f\"{'VERIFIED' if moved and back_again else 'ISSUE'}: {name} / {label} \"\n  3364\t                    f\"{'moves and comes back' if moved and back_again else 'did not behave'}\")\n  3365\t            if kind == \"page\":\n  3366\t                back()\n  3367\t    return report\n  3368\t\n  3369\t\n  3370\tdef room_is_quiet(seconds=6):\n  3371\t    \"\"\"Record for a few seconds playing NOTHING, and report what the microphone heard.\n  3372\t\n  3373\t    **THE ONE PROBE THAT SEPARATES THREE FAILURES THAT LOOK IDENTICAL.** A content check can fail\n  3374\t    because the audio never played, because it played too quietly, or because somebody in the room was\n  3375\t    talking over it — and the third is the dangerous one, since it returns a fluent, well-punctuated\n  3376\t    transcript with healthy timing that reads exactly like the product returning a wrong answer.\n  3377\t\n  3378\t    Measured 2026-09-06: a take with nothing played came back with 79 characters, and a later run asking\n  3379\t    for a German fixture returned \"Usually, yeah.\" — the founder, sitting beside his phone. Both would\n  3380\t    have been filed against the speech engine.\n  3381\t\n  3382\t    Words here mean the room is occupied, so STOP and say so rather than recording a content failure.\n  3383\t    Silence here means the room is fine and a failed content check is about the audio or the product.\n  3384\t\n  3385\t    Non-disruptive by construction: it plays nothing, so it is safe to run while somebody is talking,\n  3386\t    which is exactly when it is needed.\n  3387\t    \"\"\"\n  3388\t    if _recording_is_off():\n  3389\t        return [f\"BLOCKED: {RECORDING_IS_OFF}\"]\n  3390\t    ready()\n  3391\t    restore()\n  3392\t    clear_log()\n  3393\t    # `verify=False`: the subject is what the microphone HEARS, so the recorder's appearance is not\n  3394\t    # what this run is about, and refusing on it would refuse the probe on a phone whose pill is fine.\n  3395\t    with open_recorder(verify=False):\n  3396\t        time.sleep(seconds)\n  3397\t        stop_dictation()\n  3398\t        ending = _wait_for_the_take_to_finish(seconds=30)\n  3399\t    if ending is None:\n  3400\t        raise Blocked(\"the room probe never reached an ending, so it measured nothing\")\n  3401\t    heard = last_take()[\"transcribed_chars\"]\n  3402\t    if heard is None:\n  3403\t        raise Blocked(\"the probe ran but no transcription result was logged, so it measured nothing\")\n  3404\t    return {\n  3405\t        # Named for what was measured. Nothing recognised is good evidence the room was quiet enough\n  3406\t        # for this engine, and it is not the same claim as acoustic silence — a sound the recogniser\n  3407\t        # discards still reaches the microphone.\n  3408\t        \"quiet\": heard == 0,\n  3409\t        \"characters_heard\": heard,\n  3410\t        \"verdict\": (\"nothing was recognised with no audio played, so the room is quiet enough to test in\"\n  3411\t                    if heard == 0 else\n  3412\t                    f\"the room is OCCUPIED: {heard} characters came back with nothing played, so anything \"\n  3413\t                    \"measured now is measuring whoever is talking\"),\n  3414\t    }\n  3415\t\n  3416\t\n  3417\tdef test_dictation(sentence=\"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.\", volume=3,\n  3418\t                   record_seconds=14, target_package=\"com.android.chrome\", use_fixture=False):\n  3419\t    \"\"\"Speak into the phone and report what came back. The whole heart path, in one call.\n  3420\t\n  3421\t    **THE SHAPE IS COPIED FROM `scripts/uat/dictate-once.sh`, WHICH WORKS, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.**\n  3422\t    Between starting the take and stopping it this does exactly two things: wait, and launch the\n  3423\t    speaker. Everything else — checking the test package, reading and lowering the media volume,\n  3424\t    writing the sentence to the phone — happens BEFORE the take, and reading the screen happens after.\n  3425\t\n  3426\t    Measured 2026-09-06 against Chrome's address bar. A version that also read the recorder window\n  3427\t    (`dumpsys window windows`, several seconds) and did its staging inside the take logged\n  3428\t    `Pinned original editor package=com.android.chrome` and then, twenty-four seconds later,\n  3429\t    `No editor was pinned for this dictation; clipboard only` with `handoff=SERVICE_NOT_RUNNING`. The\n  3430\t    repository's own script, doing less, logged `handoff=SCHEDULED` on the same phone minutes later.\n  3431\t    So the harness was producing the failure, and its log read exactly like a defect in the app's\n  3432\t    insertion path.\n  3433\t\n  3434\t    **Point the phone at a real editor first.** Insertion is judged against the field the user was in,\n  3435\t    so a run started from the app's own screens is testing something the product never does. Chrome's\n  3436\t    address bar is the safe one: nothing is sent.\n  3437\t    \"\"\"\n  3438\t    if _recording_is_off():\n  3439\t        return [f\"BLOCKED: {RECORDING_IS_OFF}\"]\n  3440\t    ready()\n  3441\t    restore()\n  3442\t    if not bound():\n  3443\t        return [\"BLOCKED: auto-paste is switched off, so nothing can be inserted. \"\n  3444\t                \"enable_auto_paste() turns it back on.\"]\n  3445\t    report = []\n  3446\t\n  3447\t    def field_now():\n  3448\t        \"\"\"The target editor's IDENTITY and its text. THE ORACLE, and it is not the clipboard.\n  3449\t\n  3450\t        Publishing to the clipboard is the app's documented FALLBACK, so a clipboard check cannot tell\n  3451\t        a successful insertion from a failed one (`validation-discipline.md`\n  3452\t        RULE: verify-the-feature-not-the-crash). The editor's own text can.\n  3453\t\n  3454\t        **Identity travels with the text so the comparison is about ONE editor.** Taking \"the first\n  3455\t        EditText\" before and after lets a different field answer the second time — a screen that gains\n  3456\t        an editor, or two whose order changes — and any difference then reads as words having arrived.\n  3457\t        Prefers the FOCUSED editor, which is the one a dictation aims at.\n  3458\t        \"\"\"\n  3459\t        fields = [n for n in tree(refresh=True) if n[\"kind\"] == \"EditText\"\n  3460\t                  and (target_package is None or n[\"package\"] == target_package)]\n  3461\t        if not fields:\n  3462\t            return None\n  3463\t        focused = [n for n in fields if n[\"focused\"]]\n  3464\t        chosen = focused or fields\n  3465\t        if len(chosen) > 1:\n  3466\t            raise Blocked(\n  3467\t                f\"{len(chosen)} editors are on screen and none is uniquely focused, so which one the \"\n  3468\t                \"words were meant for is a guess\"\n  3469\t            )\n  3470\t        node = chosen[0]\n  3471\t        return (node[\"package\"], node[\"id\"] or node[\"bounds\"], node[\"text\"])\n  3472\t\n  3473\t    before = field_now()\n  3474\t    _, will_say = stage_phone_speech(sentence, volume=volume, use_fixture=use_fixture)\n  3475\t    # THE RECORDING IS AS LONG AS THE AUDIO, PLUS A MARGIN, AND NOT A ROUND NUMBER. A fixed wait leaves\n  3476\t    # the recorder running after the sound has stopped, which the founder can see and which records\n  3477\t    # whatever else is in the room. `record_seconds` stays as an override and as the answer when the\n  3478\t    # length genuinely cannot be known in advance.\n  3479\t    playing = will_say[\"seconds\"]\n  3480\t    listen_for = round(playing + TRAILING_MARGIN_S, 1) if playing else record_seconds\n  3481\t    report.append(f\"NOTE: the phone will play {will_say['what']}\"\n  3482\t                  + (f\", {playing:.1f}s long, so the take runs {listen_for:.1f}s\" if playing else \"\"))\n  3483\t    try:\n  3484\t        clear_log()\n  3485\t        # The take's whole life is this block, and the context manager closes it however the block ends.\n  3486\t        # `verify=False` because the subject here is the words, not the pill.\n  3487\t        with open_recorder(verify=False):\n  3488\t            time.sleep(LEAD_IN_S)\n  3489\t            play_staged_speech()\n  3490\t            time.sleep(listen_for)\n  3491\t            stop_dictation()\n  3492\t            ending = _wait_for_the_take_to_finish()\n  3493\t    finally:\n  3494\t        # THE MICROPHONE FIRST, the settings second, and that ordering is why the restore sits OUTSIDE\n  3495\t        # the block rather than inside it: an earlier version put the volume back before trying to close\n  3496\t        # the take, so a failure in the restore left the take running.\n  3497\t        unstage_phone_speech()\n  3498\t    if ending is None:\n  3499\t        report.append(\"ISSUE: the dictation never reached an ending, so nothing can be said about it\")\n  3500\t        return report\n  3501\t    take = last_take()\n  3502\t    report.append(f\"VERIFIED: a take ran, ended by {take['ended_by']}\" if take[\"ended_by\"]\n  3503\t                  else \"ISSUE: no take ending was logged\")\n  3504\t    if take[\"transcribed_chars\"]:\n  3505\t        report.append(f\"VERIFIED: {take['transcribed_chars']} characters came back from the speech engine\")\n  3506\t    else:\n  3507\t        report.append(\"ISSUE: nothing was transcribed. Either nothing reached the microphone, or the \"\n  3508\t                      \"speech engine returned empty.\")\n  3509\t    handoff = take[\"handoff\"]\n  3510\t    if handoff == \"SCHEDULED\":\n  3511\t        report.append(\"VERIFIED: the text was handed to the insertion path\")\n  3512\t    elif handoff:\n  3513\t        report.append(f\"ISSUE: the text did not reach the field ({handoff}); it is on the clipboard\")\n  3514\t    else:\n  3515\t        report.append(\"ISSUE: no handoff was logged at all\")\n  3516\t    # THE OUTCOME, not the request. `handoff=SCHEDULED` says the text was handed over; only the\n  3517\t    # editor's own content says it arrived. Measured 2026-09-06: a run logged SCHEDULED and then\n  3518\t    # `Editor action could not be verified after 20 attempts; clipboard only`, and the words were in\n  3519\t    # Chrome's address bar the whole time — so the log alone would have reported a working insertion\n  3520\t    # as a failure, and a clipboard check would have reported the fallback as a success.\n  3521\t    after = field_now()\n  3522\t    if after is None or before is None:\n  3523\t        report.append(\"ISSUE: no editor was on screen before or after, so where the words went is unknown\")\n  3524\t    elif after[:2] != before[:2]:\n  3525\t        report.append(\"ISSUE: a DIFFERENT editor is on screen now, so nothing here says where the words \"\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
docs/audits/2026-09-21-193-coverage.md:16:{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_7","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/zsh -lc \"wc -l .claude/knowledge/architecture.md .claude/knowledge/telemetry.md .claude/knowledge/device-testing.md; sed -n '121,320p' .claude/knowledge/architecture.md; sed -n '121,320p' .claude/knowledge/telemetry.md; sed -n '1,180p' .claude/knowledge/device-testing.md; sed -n '181,420p' .claude/knowledge/device-testing.md\"","aggregated_output":"     125 .claude/knowledge/architecture.md\n     108 .claude/knowledge/telemetry.md\n     730 .claude/knowledge/device-testing.md\n     963 total\n\nThe two auto-paste rows answer different questions and both are needed: the setting string still names a\nservice that has CRASHED. They are combined in exactly one place, the `autoPaste` derivation in\n`EnviousWisprViewModel`, and the combined answer is never stored, because `AppReadiness` is a snapshot\npushed wholesale from the Settings screen and would carry a stale liveness reading between pushes.\n# Device Testing\n\nThe phone is the only instrument that can answer most questions about this app. **Commands, ADB traps and\nGradle traps live in [`../rules/android-tooling.md`](../rules/android-tooling.md)** — this file owns the\ndevice itself and what to test on it.\n\n## FACT: the-device\n| Property | Value |\n|---|---|\n| Model | Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, `SM-S948U1`, board `canoe`, SoC SM8850 |\n| OS | Android 16, SDK 36 |\n| Accelerators | Adreno 840 GPU, Hexagon HTP NPU |\n| ADB over Tailscale | `100.94.206.47:5555` |\n| SSH into Termux | `ssh -p 8022 u0_a517@100.94.206.47` |\n\nVerified 2026-08-28. It is the founder's daily driver, not a lab device: restore any setting a session\nchanges — screen timeout, stay-awake, developer options, an accessibility service enabled for a test.\n\n## RULE: recover-the-connection-before-diagnosing-anything-else\n**Check Tailscale on the Mac first.** `adb connect` AND `ssh -p 8022` timing out together points at this\nend: `/Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale status` (`Tailscale is stopped` is the tell),\nthen `/Applications/Tailscale.app/Contents/MacOS/Tailscale up` and `~/Android/sdk/platform-tools/adb connect 100.94.206.47:5555`.\n\nWhen SSH works and ADB does not, three facts decide whether ADB is possible, in this order:\n\n| Question | How to answer it | If no |\n|---|---|---|\n| Is the phone on WiFi? | `ssh … 'ifconfig \\| grep -A1 wlan0'` | Wireless debugging needs WiFi; on cellular there is no ADB route, whatever the toggle says. |\n| Is wireless debugging on? | `ssh … 'nmap -sT -p 30000-49000 localhost -T5 --open'`, then `adb connect localhost:<port>` on each | An open port that refuses `adb connect` is not adbd. Only the founder can flip that switch. |\n| Is the port normalised? | `adb connect 100.94.206.47:5555` from the Mac | After a reboot the port is random again: `adb connect localhost:<port> && adb tcpip 5555 && adb connect localhost:5555`. |\n\n`getprop init.svc.adbd` and `sys.usb.config` read as if they answer this and do not.\n\n`android-bridge/adb-recover.sh` automates the port loop and must run ON THE PHONE\n(`ssh -p 8022 u0_a517@100.94.206.47 'bash ~/android-bridge/adb-recover.sh'`); on the Mac it fails on a\nmissing log path and a WiFi check. If it fails, SSH in, read the port under Settings, Developer options,\nWireless debugging, and run the port loop by hand. Its pidfile guard is not self-healing: if it answers \"Another instance\nrunning\" and exits 0, read `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` before killing, then remove\n`~/android-bridge/adb-recover.pid`.\n\n## RULE: a-watcher-for-the-phone-names-the-phone\n`adb devices | grep -qE \"device$\"` asks \"is A device attached\", and an emulator answers yes. Match the\nserial: `adb devices | grep -qE \"^100\\.94\\.206\\.47:5555[[:space:]]+device$\"`, with a control that the\npattern does NOT match while only the emulator is up.\n\n## RULE: connectedAndroidTest-UNINSTALLS-the-app-so-never-point-it-at-the-daily-phone\n`./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest` installs both APKs, runs, and UNINSTALLS them on the way out,\ntaking app-private storage with it: both models, the history, the custom words, every hand-granted\npermission and the saved settings, so ONBOARDING RETURNS. `scripts/hooks/command-safety.py` denies any\nGradle task named `connected*` and prints the `am instrument` form; an `ANDROID_SERIAL=emulator-*` target\nstill runs.\n\nThe symptom after the fact is `run-as: unknown package`, `pm path` printing nothing, or `am start`\nanswering `Activity class ... does not exist`. Check `pm path com.envi.wispr` FIRST. Restoring is a chore\n(twenty minutes, 1.1 GB):\n\n```bash\n$ADB -s $D install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk\n$ADB -s $D shell 'pm grant com.envi.wispr android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO'\n$ADB -s $D shell 'pm grant com.envi.wispr android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS'\n# READ the setting first and APPEND: it is a colon-separated list and this phone carries another\n# accessibility app; overwriting it turned that one off.\n$ADB -s $D shell settings get secure enabled_accessibility_services\n$ADB -s $D shell settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services \"<existing>:com.envi.wispr/com.envi.wispr.paste.PasteAccessibilityService\"\n$ADB -s $D shell settings put secure accessibility_enabled 1\n```\n\nPass that value as a tool argument, never inside a nested `adb shell '...'` string (quoted inside, it\nstored `null` and disabled every accessibility service on the phone). Then hand-place the models per\n[model-delivery.md](model-delivery.md) PROCEDURE: place-a-model-by-hand. All four steps proven\n2026-08-31. Prefer a manual ADB run for a single question; reach for `connectedAndroidTest` only when the\nrig is genuinely the subject, on the emulator.\n\n**`am instrument` is not safe by itself: READ THE SUITE'S `@Before` FIRST.** `AndroidKeystoreSecretStoreTest.setUp`\nDELETES `no_backup/provider-secrets.v1` unconditionally and `ProviderConfigurationRepositoryTest.setUp`\nclears the real provider preferences, so either class on the founder's phone destroys his hand-entered\nkeys. Storage and Keystore suites ask nothing of the microphone, NPU, side button or a real editor: run\nthem on `emulator-5554`.\n\n## RULE: drive-the-instrumented-tests-with-am-instrument-not-gradle\n`am instrument` does not uninstall, so it is the way to run a device test against the founder's phone:\n\n```bash\nADB=~/Android/sdk/platform-tools/adb\nD=100.94.206.47:5555\n./gradlew :app:assembleDebug :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest\n$ADB -s $D install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk\n$ADB -s $D install -r -t app/build/outputs/apk/androidTest/debug/app-debug-androidTest.apk   # -t: test-only\n$ADB -s $D shell 'am instrument -w -e class com.envi.wispr.VoicePipelineDeviceTest#<method> \\\n    com.envi.wispr.test/androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner'\n```\n\n- **Re-enable accessibility after EVERY `install -r`** (it unbinds the service and clears\n  `enabled_accessibility_services`); set it back, wait a few seconds, never in the same breath as the install.\n- **Generate the spoken audio with Azure Speech** (`~/.claude/knowledge/ai/cloud-llm-credits.md`, voice\n  `en-US-AvaNeural`, `X-Microsoft-OutputFormat: raw-16khz-16bit-mono-pcm` is exactly the headerless\n  fixture format). Write it to BOTH `com.envi.wispr` and `com.envi.wispr.test` under `cache/enviouswispr-uat.pcm`.\n- **`VoicePipelineDeviceTest` REPORTS THE POLISHED TEXT, NOT THE TRANSCRIPT** (`polishedText` is ASR,\n  cleanup, then S1-mini). To measure a stage, bind `:asr` directly in a throwaway probe and fail an\n  assertion carrying `RAW=[...] CLEANED=[...]` (the fixture is our own TTS, so the content rule is not in\n  play); delete the probe afterwards.\n- **Parakeet v3 does its own number and currency formatting** (`$37,200`, `64 gigabytes`); never\n  attribute a formatted number to our code without the raw line.\n- **Known stale assertion:** `launcherRecordsPhonePlaybackAndReachesClipboardStep` requires `(NPU)` in\n  the polish log; this phone reports `(GPU)`, so the row goes red after a dictation that worked.\n\n## FACT: the-ASSIST-action-opens-a-CHOOSER-on-this-phone\n`am start -a android.intent.action.ASSIST` does NOT start the recorder on the S26. It shows Android's\n\"Complete action using\" chooser, because more than one app answers the action and no default is set.\nFounder observed it 2026-08-30 with the dialog on his screen. Launch the component instead:\n\n```bash\n$ADB shell 'am start -n com.envi.wispr/.ui.VoiceInputActivity'\n```\n\nA missing microphone or notification permission sends that activity straight to Settings and no session\nstarts, which reads exactly like the launch failing. Check `dumpsys package com.envi.wispr | grep granted`\nbefore diagnosing anything else.\n\n## FACT: uiautomator-dump-crashes-on-this-phone-INTERMITTENTLY\n`adb shell uiautomator dump` failed on this Android 16 / One UI build on 2026-09-01 with `RC=137` and no XML, logcat\npointing at `UiAutomationShellWrapper.connect()`, with or without any accessibility service bound (so not a\nservice conflict). The same day a dozen-plus calls succeeded, so it CAN fail, not DOES fail: `tree()`\nretries, and after a second 137 answers `Blocked` naming `shot()`, `overlay()` and `last_take()` as the\neyes that still work (RULE: no-appium-and-no-tap-by-position).\n\n## RULE: drive-the-phone-with-wispr-eyes\n`scripts/uat/wispr_eyes.py` is the default way to see and drive the app; the one document for it is\n`../skills/wispr-eyes/SKILL.md`, its own tests `python3 scripts/uat/test_wispr_eyes.py`. Recording from\nit is OFF for the PHYSICAL phone (`RECORDING_IS_OFF`, scoped by `_recording_is_off()` since #177; the\nemulator records); delete that constant only on a review round whose verdict says the take-with-no-debt\nCLASS is closed. Since #177 it is the only door: raw driving commands are refused by\n`scripts/hooks/command-safety.py` (`../rules/tools-and-apps.md` RULE:\ndrive-the-phone-through-wispr-eyes-before-any-raw-adb). Redirect a long run through `python3 -u`, or a backgrounded\n`scan()` writes an empty file for minutes. **After `adb install -r`, force-stop through `stop_app()`, never raw\n`am force-stop`:** a raw force-stop clears the accessibility baseline, `enable_auto_paste()` then journals that\ncleared state as the debt, and `dictate_emulator()` starts with `restore()`, which pays the debt back and reports\nauto-paste off (2026-09-20). `stop_app()` journals the on state first and settles its own debt.\n\n```bash\npython3 scripts/uat/wispr_eyes.py look        # what is on screen\npython3 scripts/uat/wispr_eyes.py scan        # every screen, every switch\npython3 scripts/uat/wispr_eyes.py restore     # put the phone back\npython3 -c \"import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts/uat'); from wispr_eyes import *; print(switches())\"\n```\n\n**Four eyes, and two see the recorder** (measured 2026-09-06 and 2026-09-20, service bound, take running):\n\n| Eye | Sees the app's pages | Sees the floating recorder | Cost |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| the FAST eye: the app's own accessibility service through `DebugDumpReceiver` (`tree()` on a DEBUG build with the service bound; #181) | YES, every window: app, keyboard, status bar, our bubble | YES: `Recording controls`, the clock, Cancel, Stop, as nodes | 0.1 s |\n| the SLOW eye: `uiautomator dump` (`tree()` on a release build or an unbound service) | YES | NO, zero nodes while the pill was on screen | 1.9 s, all of it process start |\n| `screencap` (`shot()`) | YES, as pixels | NO, the home screen with no pill | ~1 s |\n| `dumpsys window windows` (`overlay()`) | geometry only | YES: `EnviousWispr recording controls`, `shown`, `HAS_DRAWN`, `isOnScreen`, `isVisible` reported separately | 0.1 s |\n\nThe fast eye refreshes every node from the live view before reading it: the service's node cache\nreported a switch's OLD state for 1.5 s after a tap (2026-09-20). It reads mid-animation, so anything\nthat turns a reading into a coordinate reads through `_stable_tree()` (two identical reads 0.12 s\napart). Only the shell can ask it (`android.permission.DUMP`); a second debuggable package gets nothing.\n\nAsk the tree about a PAGE, `overlay()` about the RECORDER, and the LOG (`recording()` reads\n`recording_start` against `recording_stop` from `AudioCapture`) about the take. Never tap the pill by a\ncoordinate: `stop_dictation()` / `cancel_dictation()` use `VoiceInputActivity`'s exported `stop` and\n`cancel` extras. `dumpsys notification` keeps our entry after the take ends and is not a witness. A\nscreenshot cannot answer anything about the recorder, including its level meter: the region belongs to\nthe app behind the pill. Whether the meter responds is a question for a screen RECORDING.\n\n## FACT: force-stopping-the-app-CLEARS-the-accessibility-permission\nMeasured 2026-09-06: a force-stop CLEARS `Settings.Secure.enabled_accessibility_services` (`setting=null`\nafterwards), so the user's grant is erased and nothing restores it; every dictation then lands on the\nclipboard. A force-stop reaches real users (app info, a task killer, Samsung's \"put unused apps to sleep\");\nissue #131 owns the product side. Repair, and read `bound()` back rather than the setting string:\n\n```bash\n$ADB shell settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services com.envi.wispr/com.envi.wispr.paste.PasteAccessibilityService\n$ADB shell settings put secure accessibility_enabled 1\n```\n\n`wispr_eyes.stop_app()` repairs after its own force-stops; `enable_auto_paste()` is the repair alone.\n\n## FACT: scrolling-UP-from-near-the-top-pulls-down-the-notification-shade\nA drag that starts in the top strip opens the notification shade, and every later step then reports\n`EnviousWispr is not on screen; showing com.android.systemui`. Start any downward drag below the top sixth\nof the screen (`wispr_eyes.scroll` clamps it); `cmd statusbar collapse` closes a shade and is allowed where\na swipe at a keyguard is not.\n\n## RULE: choose-a-control-by-ANCESTRY-never-by-which-box-surrounds-it\nCompose puts a row's words and its behaviour on different nodes: `SettingsToggleRow` writes its title into\na `TextView` and its state onto the `toggleable` Row that CONTAINS it. Find the words, then walk UP THE\nPARSED TREE (`wispr_eyes.tree()` records each node's `parent`; `_holder` walks it), never \"the smallest\nclickable box whose bounds enclose the label\", because an overlapping control gives the wrong answer and\nthis harness presses buttons that delete a 484 MB model. A flat test fixture cannot catch this; write\nfixtures nested the way the phone reports them.\n\n## RULE: a-change-to-the-phone-must-outlive-the-command-that-made-it\n`wispr_eyes` runs one process per errand, so the \"put it back\" book is a FILE,\n`~/.cache/wispr-eyes/restore.json`, keyed by device serial, written BEFORE the change and cleared only\nafter the restore was read back. A running take is a change in that book, written before the start intent\nand settled after the microphone closes, so any later session's `restore()` ends it.\n\n```bash\ncat ~/.cache/wispr-eyes/restore.json\npython3 -c \"import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/uat'); from wispr_eyes import *; print(restore())\"\n```\n\n## RULE: no-appium-and-no-tap-by-position\nAppium left this project on 2026-09-20 (#177): a UiAutomator2 session holds `UiAutomation`, which unbinds\nthe accessibility service that draws the recorder and inserts text, so every dictation under it hands off\n`SERVICE_NOT_RUNNING`. The harness's eyes replace it (`look()`, `find()`, `overlay()`, `shot()`), and when\n`uiautomator dump` dies twice with 137 the answer is `Blocked` naming those, never a second reader.\n\n**Never tap a control by position.** A clickable ancestor carries no `text`; the label is in a child. A\nsession that inferred \"Refresh\" from position deleted the founder's OpenAI key. **Never press Remove on\nhis phone unless removing is the thing under test** (founder 2026-09-02); a key is not dev state.\nRestoring one is possible from GCP (`~/.claude/bin/get-key launch openai-api-key K -- ...`), but the\nLadder then auto-saves and switches polish to that provider, so the repair changes his settings too.\n`tap('label')` resolves by words; the Bash hook refuses a raw `input tap`.\n\n## FACT: samsung-keyboard-can-float-a-clipboard-suggestion-over-an-inline-button\nThe Samsung keyboard can draw a floating clipboard-suggestion chip above a focused field when the\nclipboard holds content resembling what is typed (seen with a password-type field, #62, 2026-09-01). It\nrenders in the IME layer ABOVE the app and intercepts taps meant for an in-field control such as this\napp's \"Check\". Dismiss it (tap its ✕) or avoid copying test values to the clipboard. Separately, a raw\n`input tap` within about 50 px of the right edge can trigger an OS gesture instead; keep synthetic taps\naway from the outer edge margin, and take bounds from a page source, never from screenshot pixels.\n\n## RULE: one-phone-serialises-every-session\nThere is exactly one device and Codex drives it too. Before a device run, check whether something else is\non it — `dumpsys package com.envi.wispr | grep lastUpdateTime` tells you whether a different build was just\ninstalled. Two sessions installing different builds onto one phone produce results that belong to neither.\n\n## FACT: insertion-is-IMPOSSIBLE-on-a-locked-phone-and-here-is-the-proof\nWhile the phone is secure-locked the accessibility service sees exactly one window, the keyguard, and no\napplication window (measured 2026-09-03: `dumpsys accessibility` shows `type=TYPE_SYSTEM` only and zero\n`envi.wispr.test` windows with the service BOUND and `PasteTargetActivity` top-resumed). Capture, the\ndetector, auto-stop, transcription and polish all run locked, and a fixture with `android:showWhenLocked`\nplays audio into the microphone; only the last hop is unreachable. **Read the bound count before believing\nany window count**: an unbound service also reports zero windows. `dumpsys accessibility | grep -c \"Bound\nservices:{Service\\[label=EnviousWispr\"` first; a bare re-`put` of the same setting string does NOT rebind.\n\n## FACT: a-locked-screen-is-a-real-blocker-not-an-occupancy-question\n`dumpsys power | grep mWakefulness` reports `Dozing` or `Asleep` when the phone's own screen timeout has\nlocked it, distinct from the founder actively using it. `KEYCODE_WAKEUP` lights the screen but does not\nbypass a secure lock; `dumpsys deviceidle | grep mScreenLocked` confirms whether it is still locked.\nMeasured 2026-08-31: a UAT session's `am start` and tap landed silently on the lock screen mid-run.\n\nThis is not the \"never wait for Saurabh\" case in `../rules/tools-and-apps.md`. That rule is about not\npausing for his own use of an unlocked phone; a secure lock needs his PIN, which the harness does not have\nand must never try to guess. Check wakefulness before trusting a tap or screenshot, and if locked, report\n`NEED YOU` and stop rather than sending input into a black screen.\n\n## RULE: the-emulator-cannot-answer-the-questions-that-matter\n`scripts/enviouswispr-emulator.sh` boots an AVD and installs the debug APK. Use it for Compose layout,\nnavigation and permission flows; it cannot answer anything about the vendor runtime, the Samsung side\nbutton, Samsung window layering, battery, or thermals, and a latency claim measured there is not evidence.\n**Emulator FIRST for screen-only work** (founder 2026-09-01: \"stop using my phone for testing\"): a\nchange that touches no capture, ASR, polish engine, insertion or model-loading code validates on the\nemulator and takes the phone only for a question the emulator cannot answer; a plan's hardware UAT section\nfor a screen-only change names the emulator.\n\n**It CAN hear speech and HAS real editors** (Chrome, Messages, Gmail, Gboard on `EnviousWispr_Android_16`;\nSamsung-specific behaviour is not testable). Two switches gate the microphone: `-allow-host-audio` on the\nlaunch line PERMITS it, and `adb -s emulator-5554 emu avd hostmicon` turns it ON (not persisted; without\nit every take records silence and `AsrService` logs `textChars=0` while the pipeline reports success).\n`scripts/enviouswispr-emulator.sh` runs `hostmicon` on every launch. The canonical audio feed is RULE:\nfeed-emulator-audio-over-grpc-injectaudio-not-blackhole; the cable path (`say_into_emulator()`,\n`SwitchAudioSource -t input -s \"BlackHole 2ch\"`, `say -a \"BlackHole 2ch\"`, needs `brew install\nblackhole-2ch switchaudio-osx`) is the fallback, and the speaker path is retired (founder 2026-09-13).\nTwo traps: `adb emu kill` takes up to 20 s to release the microphone, and an emulator launched inside that\nwindow logs `coreaudio: Could not initialize record` and hears nothing until relaunched; the launch script\nbackgrounds the emulator, so run it with `run_in_background`. Parakeet is placed by PROCEDURE:\nplace-a-model-by-hand (`model-delivery.md`).\n\n## FACT: the-lips-bubble-uat\nThe floating lips button (#135, PR #137) was exercised on the emulator with these probes on 2026-09-12:\n`emulator-5556` (AVD `EnviousWispr_Bubble`, Android 16, Gboard, Chrome, `-allow-host-audio`), debug build\nof `feat/135-lips-bubble-on-brand` at `25a9ac6` (the same three commits, copied off the onboarding branch onto #119). Reset the\ndock with `run-as com.envi.wispr rm shared_prefs/lips_bubble_position.xml` and `am kill com.envi.wispr`.\n\n## FACT: the-earbud-colour-uat\nThe blue earbud lips (#171, build 140, founder pass 2026-09-18 \"yes works great\") are a phone-only check;\nthe emulator has no Bluetooth. The colour's input is on\nlogcat as `PasteService: Bubble colour: inputs=N earbuds=true|false`; the History card's microphone\nline is the independent check of what recorded.\n\nWhat rung 1 on the Play AVD taught (2026-09-18): `WISPR_SERIAL=emulator-5554` points the harness at the\nemulator; the AVD unlock recipe lives in `../skills/wispr-eyes/SKILL.md` \"The emulator\"; a `data:` URL\nhanded to `am start` is re-parsed by the device shell, and Chrome refuses `file:///sdcard/...`\n(`ERR_ACCESS_DENIED`), so the editor is Gmail compose through the harness (`tap('Compose',\npackage='com.google.android.gm')` then `focus_field('Compose email', 'com.google.android.gm')`);\ndiscard the draft afterwards through `More options` then `Discard`. `settings put secure\nenabled_accessibility_services \"\"` is \"Bad arguments\"; set the component directly.\n\n## FACT: the-microphone-swap-uat\nThe Mac-style swap (#173, build 142, founder pass 2026-09-18 \"ran the gambit - works great\") needs two\nheadsets, so it is phone-only. Recipe: pick the AirPods in Settings → AirPods off, Bose \"Storm\" on →\nMicrophone page: Auto selected, \"Using Storm\", no AirPods row → dictate: no AirPods line on the recorder\n(the one Bluetooth tip may show), History card \"Microphone: Storm\" → AirPods on: the AirPods row is back\nand selected → tap Storm; AirPods on: AirPods listed, not selected (the memory was replaced) → both off:\nAuto, \"Using Phone\" → leave and reopen Settings: rows right on open → tap the already-selected Auto row,\nStorm on: Auto stays (memory gone). Oracle: the rows by eye and the History card's microphone line; on\nlogcat `AudioCapture: route start=<device> ... reason=PICKED|AUTO|PICK_MISSING` says what the take chose.\n\nTwo connection lessons from that run. The phone's log keeps about an hour (`logcat -G` is capped at 5 MiB\non the S26), so a finding reported later than that has no log: start `adb logcat -v time AudioCapture:V\nDictationSession:V AsrService:V PasteService:V '*:S' > <file>` on the Mac in the background BEFORE the\nfounder's run. And after Wireless debugging is re-enabled the phone can appear only as an mDNS serial\n(`adb-R5GL11DR0EZ-…._adb-tls-connect._tcp`, sometimes with a ` (N)` suffix, so match it with a pattern):\n`adb -s \"<that serial>\" tcpip 5555` then `adb connect 100.94.206.47:5555` normalises it; the four ports\n`nmap` shows open on the phone were not adbd.\n\n## FACT: the-insertion-uat-matrix\nUnit tests and the paste-target fixture cannot close the insertion contract. The matrix, driven by the\nside button with Gboard the default keyboard: a plain field (Messages); a rich editor (Gmail, Google\nDocs); a browser field (Chrome address bar, a web form); a terminal or code editor; a chat app; a password\nfield, treated as ordinary by decision (`../rules/architecture-rules.md` FACT:\nthere-is-no-sensitive-field-guard-and-that-is-decided; until #11 lands it still diverts to copy-only, so\nthat row proves the OLD behaviour); a stale or unsupported target, which must keep the transcript on the\nclipboard and say so; and **back-to-back** (dictate, insert, immediately dictate again, asserting the\nsecond transcript reaches the editor), where the P1 lives (#132).\n\n## FACT: what-gmail-actually-does-to-insertion-2026-08-30\nMeasured on the S26 from the founder's own dictations. Four symptoms, one cause.\n\n- **The insertion succeeds and is reported as unverified.** All 21 attempts logged `action=SET_TEXT\n  textMatched=true ... caret=0/0 expectedCaret=34`; the only failing clause in\n  `AccessibilityInsertionRules.isVerified` is the caret, because Gmail's compose reports `0/0` wherever\n  the insertion went. **The caret is NOT cosmetic, so do not drop it from the check**: it decides WHERE the\n  words go, and a `0/0` read puts them at the start of the field (\"it also sucks other text to it\").\n- **It destroys the user's whitespace.** `SET_TEXT` replaces the WHOLE field with a string composed from a\n  lossy read-back (`AccessibilityNodeInfo.text` normalises whitespace), so lines merge. Do NOT relax\n  `isVerified`; a check that accepted this ships silent data loss in real drafts.\n- **Why the destructive path was taken:** `normalizedSelection` returns `null` for `-1/-1` and the code\n  fell back to paste on that null, but Gmail reports `0/0`, a PLAUSIBLE value, not a sentinel\n  (`../rules/validation-discipline.md` FACT: silent-empty-traps). The log corroborates: `ACTION_SET_SELECTION`\n  to 34 followed by a read of `0/0`, so this editor reports no caret at all.\n- Closing and reopening Gmail fixes it, so the app works from a stale view of that editor.\n\nResolved by #141's one-route-one-write rule (commit route, then paste, no `ACTION_SET_TEXT`); the macOS\ncascade for comparison is `Sources/EnviousWisprPipeline/PasteCascadeExecutor.swift`, and the two shipping\ncompetitors neither check the caret nor rewrite a non-empty compose\n(`docs/internal/competitor-insertion-study.md`). **Reproducing it needs the founder's own hand:** every\nGmail compose opened over ADB reported `NO_PINNED_TARGET`, so two runs are comparable only when the\neditor was opened the same way.\n\n## FACT: the-141-one-write-emulator-uat\nRun 2026-09-13 on `emulator-5554` (`EnviousWispr_Android_16`, Gboard, Chrome, host mic on). Editor: a\nlocal page from the Mac (`http://10.0.2.2:8765`) with a `<textarea>` holding two paragraphs and a blank\nline, and a mirror `<pre>` showing `JSON.stringify(value)`. Oracle: the mirror, never the clipboard or log.\n\nChunk 1 (debug build of `feat/141-insertion-cascade` at `52ef940`, paste only): two takes, both `route=PASTE ...\noutcome=VERIFIED` (attempts 2 then 14, the second because Chrome's node lagged the paste), blank line\nintact, each sentence once at the caret with the seam space. Capitals and the trailing period come from\nthe cleanup limb. `Clipboard changed during insertion; preserving the newer clipboard` after a success is\n`ClipboardService: Denying clipboard access ... not in focus` (the Android 10+ background read limit), so\nthe user's previous clip is not restored.\n\nChunk 2 (`feat/141-commit-route` at `2fe39dc`, voice through the cable): four dictations, every line\n`route=COMMIT written=true returned=VOID outcome=VERIFIED` (caret after \"Hi team,\", end of draft,\nmid-draft right after an `adb install -r`, and a short mid-draft take with `evidence=SURROUNDING`), no\nclipboard write, seam and capital right. Log shapes: `Input started on the pipe: package=... restarting=true`\nat every focus change; `Commit route not eligible: <reason>` (`no input method`, `input not started`,\n`session package differs`, `focused window differs`, `pinned editor not focused`) when paste is taken;\n`The pipe read surrounding text: before=<n> after=<n> offset=<n>`. Chrome answers `offset=-1` (unknown), so\na window shorter than the compare length hands over to the node judge (`evidence=NODE`), while a payload\nshort enough for the window verifies by the windows (`evidence=SURROUNDING`). The service's own `withPinnedNode` proof is the\neligibility test, not a FOCUS_INPUT search from the window root.      1	package com.envi.wispr.paste
     2	
     3	import android.graphics.Rect
     4	import android.view.accessibility.AccessibilityNodeInfo
     5	import android.view.accessibility.AccessibilityWindowInfo
     6	
     7	/**
     8	 * The accessibility tree as the XML `uiautomator dump` writes, from the windows this service already
     9	 * holds (#181). The test harness (`scripts/uat/wispr_eyes.py`) parses exactly these attributes; a
    10	 * `uiautomator dump` costs 1.9 s of process start per read, this costs milliseconds and, unlike
    11	 * `uiautomator`, sees the service's own accessibility overlay.
    12	 *
    13	 * Pure: the walk is over [TreeNode], an interface the unit tests fake, and [fromWindows] is the only
    14	 * line that touches the framework. Every string attribute goes through one escaper, because the
    15	 * value that breaks the XML is never the one a test happened to try.
    16	 */
    17	internal object WindowTreeXml {
    18	    /** One node of an accessibility tree, in the shape the harness reads. */
    19	    interface TreeNode {
    20	        val text: String
    21	        val description: String
    22	        val packageName: String
    23	        val className: String
    24	        val viewId: String
    25	        val clickable: Boolean
    26	        val enabled: Boolean
    27	        val selected: Boolean
    28	        val scrollable: Boolean
    29	        val focused: Boolean
    30	        val checkable: Boolean
    31	        val checked: Boolean
    32	        /** left, top, right, bottom on screen. */
    33	        val bounds: IntArray
    34	        val children: List<TreeNode>
    35	    }
    36	
    37	    fun render(roots: List<TreeNode>): String {
    38	        val out = StringBuilder("<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8' standalone='yes' ?>")
    39	        out.append("<hierarchy rotation=\"0\">")
    40	        roots.forEach { appendNode(out, it) }
    41	        out.append("</hierarchy>")
    42	        return out.toString()
    43	    }
    44	
    45	    private fun appendNode(out: StringBuilder, node: TreeNode) {
    46	        val b = node.bounds
    47	        out.append("<node")
    48	        attr(out, "text", node.text)
    49	        attr(out, "resource-id", node.viewId)
    50	        attr(out, "class", node.className)
    51	        attr(out, "package", node.packageName)
    52	        attr(out, "content-desc", node.description)
    53	        attr(out, "checkable", node.checkable.toString())
    54	        attr(out, "checked", node.checked.toString())
    55	        attr(out, "clickable", node.clickable.toString())
    56	        attr(out, "enabled", node.enabled.toString())
    57	        attr(out, "focused", node.focused.toString())
    58	        attr(out, "scrollable", node.scrollable.toString())
    59	        attr(out, "selected", node.selected.toString())
    60	        attr(out, "bounds", "[${b[0]},${b[1]}][${b[2]},${b[3]}]")
    61	        if (node.children.isEmpty()) {
    62	            out.append(" />")
    63	            return
    64	        }
    65	        out.append(">")
    66	        node.children.forEach { appendNode(out, it) }
    67	        out.append("</node>")
    68	    }
    69	
    70	    private fun attr(out: StringBuilder, name: String, value: String) {
    71	        out.append(' ').append(name).append("=\"").append(escape(value)).append('"')
    72	    }
    73	
    74	    /** XML attribute escaping for every string attribute: the five markup characters and control codes. */
    75	    fun escape(value: String): String {
    76	        val out = StringBuilder(value.length + 8)
    77	        for (c in value) {
    78	            when {
    79	                c == '&' -> out.append("&amp;")
    80	                c == '<' -> out.append("&lt;")
    81	                c == '>' -> out.append("&gt;")
    82	                c == '"' -> out.append("&quot;")
    83	                c == '\'' -> out.append("&apos;")
    84	                c == '\n' || c == '\t' || c == '\r' -> out.append(c)
    85	                c < ' ' -> out.append(' ')
    86	                else -> out.append(c)
    87	            }
    88	        }
    89	        return out.toString()
    90	    }
    91	
    92	    /**
    93	     * The framework adapter: every window's root, walked depth first. A window with no root is
    94	     * skipped; a child that cannot be read is skipped. Nothing here recycles: the API floor is 33,
    95	     * where `AccessibilityNodeInfo.recycle` is a no-op.
    96	     */
    97	    fun fromWindows(windows: List<AccessibilityWindowInfo>): List<TreeNode> =
    98	        windows.mapNotNull { window -> window.root?.let { adapt(it, depth = 0) } }
    99	
   100	    private const val MAX_DEPTH = 64
   101	
   102	    private fun adapt(info: AccessibilityNodeInfo, depth: Int): TreeNode? {
   103	        // THE CACHE LIES AFTER A TAP. The service's node cache is invalidated by the events it
   104	        // subscribes to, and a switch flipping emits none of them, so a walk read right after a tap
   105	        // reported the OLD checked state for seconds (measured 2026-09-20: fast eye False, uiautomator
   106	        // True, for 1.5 s). `refresh()` asks the app's view directly. A node that is gone answers
   107	        // false and is dropped.
   108	        if (!info.refresh()) return null
   109	        val rect = Rect()
   110	        info.getBoundsInScreen(rect)
   111	        val kids = if (depth >= MAX_DEPTH) emptyList() else
   112	            (0 until info.childCount).mapNotNull { i -> info.getChild(i)?.let { adapt(it, depth + 1) } }
   113	        return Snapshot(
   114	            text = info.text?.toString().orEmpty(),
   115	            description = info.contentDescription?.toString().orEmpty(),
   116	            packageName = info.packageName?.toString().orEmpty(),
   117	            className = info.className?.toString().orEmpty(),
   118	            viewId = info.viewIdResourceName.orEmpty(),
   119	            clickable = info.isClickable,
   120	            enabled = info.isEnabled,
   121	            selected = info.isSelected,
   122	            scrollable = info.isScrollable,
   123	            focused = info.isFocused,
   124	            checkable = info.isCheckable,
   125	            checked = info.isChecked,
   126	            bounds = intArrayOf(rect.left, rect.top, rect.right, rect.bottom),
   127	            children = kids,
   128	        )
   129	    }
   130	
   131	    /** A value copy of a node, taken while the framework object is live. */
   132	    class Snapshot(
   133	        override val text: String,
   134	        override val description: String,
   135	        override val packageName: String,
   136	        override val className: String,
   137	        override val viewId: String,
   138	        override val clickable: Boolean,
   139	        override val enabled: Boolean,
   140	        override val selected: Boolean,
   141	        override val scrollable: Boolean,
   142	        override val focused: Boolean,
   143	        override val checkable: Boolean,
   144	        override val checked: Boolean,
   145	        override val bounds: IntArray,
   146	        override val children: List<TreeNode>,
   147	    ) : TreeNode
   148	}
   105	
   106	    fun isExpectedWindow(
   107	        packageName: String?,
   108	        windowId: Int,
   109	        expectedPackageName: String,
   110	        expectedWindowId: Int,
   111	    ): Boolean = packageName == expectedPackageName && windowId == expectedWindowId
   112	
   113	    /**
   114	     * Android may expose an empty editor's hint through node.text. It is not user content.
   115	     *
   116	     * This fold is for the PRE-WRITE snapshot and for composing the smart payload only. The judge takes
   117	     * the raw [EditorRead] on both sides, because a hint AFTER the write is not "the field is empty",
   118	     * it is "the words are not visible", which is a different answer.
   119	     */
   120	    fun observableEditorText(text: CharSequence?, isShowingHintText: Boolean): String =
   121	        if (isShowingHintText) "" else text?.toString().orEmpty()
   122	
   123	    /** The baseline a pre-write read establishes: `""` for a hint, the text otherwise, null when unread. */
   124	    fun baseline(read: EditorRead): String? = if (read.isShowingHintText) "" else read.text
   125	
   126	    /**
   127	     * The ONE way a node read becomes the `(baseline, selection)` pair the paste route composes against
   128	     * and compares at the write boundary. Two call sites deriving it separately disagreed on a null
   129	     * text (one kept null, one folded it to `""`), which made every boundary check report a changed
   130	     * context on editors that expose no text (Codex code review round 9).

    16	## 0. TL;DR
    17	The harness stops passing on weak evidence: a take's verdict requires the current take's own `insertion api=` line with `outcome=VERIFIED`, `written=true` and the right target, reports the route (COMMIT or PASTE) as its own line, compares the editor's WHOLE final text with an explicit expected value, accepts only a uniquely FOCUSED editor as the target, reads `bound()` from the whole bound-services block, bounds its log reads to the take it owns, keys its restore book by the phone's hardware identity, says `NOT RUN` (never `BLOCKED`) when recording is off, and can wrap a take in an owned, journaled screen recording. The dormant speaker-playback path (`stage_phone_speech` and friends, the windowed `SpeakerPlaybackActivity` launch) is deleted from the harness, superseded by #162's silent injector on the phone and gRPC on the emulator; the proposed test-APK playback Service is not built. `VoicePipelineDeviceTest` stops sleeping and polling logcat: its two take rows wait on the session owner's phase writes and the History row's insertion outcome, assert the destination editor's whole text from the editor's own receipt file, exactly once, the non-target editor unchanged, and the stored route; the audio is fed by the driver (harness) when the test reports LISTENING, on the emulator over gRPC and on the phone through the #162 injector, so the test itself never plays a speaker. A two-editor side-button row (REF-01) joins it.
    18	

codex
The driver/test stream is sound: `sendStatus` reaches the system instrumentation watcher immediately, and raw `am instrument -r` prints the bundle and status code before the test finishes. The remaining substantive gap is in `dictate_emulator`: `open_recorder(verify=False)` currently waits only fixed sleeps, not the owner’s live signal.
